title.raw: 卷一百七十九 志第一百三十二 食貨下一 Volume 179 Treatises 132: Finance and Economics 2a

sentences.zh: 食貨下一

translations.literal: Finance and Goods, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Two

sentences.zh: （會計）〉

translations.literal: (Accounting) closing mark〉
translations.idiomatic: (Accounting) closing mark〉

sentences.zh: 宋貨財之製，多因於唐。

translations.literal: The Song system for goods and wealth largely followed that of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Song institutions governing wealth and commodities largely inherited those of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以後，天下多事，戶口凋耗，租稅日削，法既變而用不給，故興利者進，而征斂名額繁矣。

translations.literal: From after the Tianbao era, the realm had many troubles; household registers withered; land tax was cut day by day; though laws had changed, use was not supplied; therefore those who sought profit advanced, and the names and quotas of levies and exactions grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao reign, the empire was beset by turmoil: registered households declined, land tax revenues shrank steadily, and repeated legal reforms still failed to meet expenditure. Profit-seeking officials rose in influence, and the roster of taxes and exactions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 方鎮握重兵，皆留財賦自贍，其上供殊鮮。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioners held heavy troops; all retained fiscal revenues to support themselves; what they forwarded upward was especially scant.
translations.idiomatic: Regional military governors controlled large armies, kept tax revenues for their own support, and sent very little to the central government.

sentences.zh: 五代疆境逼蹙，藩鎮益強，率令部曲主場、院，其屬三司者，補大吏以臨之，輸額之外亦私有焉。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties the borders were cramped and pressed; the regional governors grew stronger; they generally ordered their retainers to manage markets and monopoly offices; where these belonged to the Three Departments, they supplemented great officials to oversee them; beyond the delivery quota they also privately possessed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, as territory shrank, regional governors grew more powerful. They usually placed their own retainers in charge of markets and monopoly bureaus; even where an office fell under the Three Departments, they posted senior men to supervise it and kept for themselves whatever exceeded the official quota.

sentences.zh: 太祖周知其弊，及受命，務恢遠略，修建法程，示之以漸。

translations.literal: Taizu thoroughly knew these abuses; when he received the Mandate, he devoted himself to restoring a far-reaching plan, built up legal procedures, and showed it to them gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu understood these abuses well. Once he took the throne, he set about restoring long-range policy, strengthening the legal framework, and introducing reform step by step.

sentences.zh: 建隆中，牧守來朝，猶不貢奉以助軍實。

translations.literal: In the Jianlong period, prefects and governors who came to court still did not present tribute to help military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: As late as the Jianlong era, prefects and governors attending court still did not send tribute to bolster military stores.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，始詔諸州支度經費外，凡金帛悉送闕下，毋或占留。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, it was first decreed that beyond each prefecture's budgeted expenses, all gold and silk were to be sent to the court, and none were to be retained.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 3, an edict for the first time required every prefecture, after meeting its budgeted expenses, to send all gold and silk to the capital with no local retention.

sentences.zh: 時藩郡有闕，稍命文臣權知所在場務，或遣京朝官廷臣監臨。

translations.literal: At that time, when a regional prefecture had a vacancy, civil officials were gradually ordered to act as temporary managers of local market offices, or capital court officials were sent to supervise on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When a post in a former regional command fell vacant, the court increasingly assigned civil officials to manage local revenue offices on a provisional basis, or dispatched capital officials to supervise them directly.

sentences.zh: 於是外權始削，而利歸公上，條禁文簿漸為精密。

translations.literal: Thereupon outside power began to be cut, profit returned to the public fisc, and regulations, prohibitions, and account books gradually became precise and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Regional power was thus pared back, revenue flowed to the central treasury, and regulations and account books grew steadily more exact.

sentences.zh: 諸州通判官到任，皆須躬閱帳籍所列官物，吏不得以售其奸。

translations.literal: When the general-assessor officials of the prefectures took office, all had personally to review the official goods listed in the account books, so clerks could not sell their deceit.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, each prefectural general assessor had to inspect the official goods recorded in the ledgers in person, so clerks could not conceal fraud.

sentences.zh: 主庫吏三年一易。

translations.literal: The chief warehouse clerks were changed once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Warehouse chiefs were rotated every three years.

sentences.zh: 市征、地課、鹽曲之類，通判官、兵馬都監、縣令等並親臨之，見月籍供三司，秩滿較其殿最，欺隱者寘於法。

translations.literal: Market levies, land dues, salt and yeast monopolies, and the like—the general assessors, military inspectors, and magistrates all personally attended to them; monthly registers were submitted to the Three Departments; at the end of their terms their performance was compared, and those who concealed or deceived were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Market taxes, land dues, salt and liquor monopolies, and similar revenues had to be overseen in person by general assessors, military inspectors, and magistrates. Monthly registers went to the Three Departments; at term's end officials were ranked on performance, and concealment was prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 募告者，賞錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Those who were recruited to inform were rewarded with three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Informants were offered a reward of three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 而小民求財報怨，訴訟煩擾，未幾，除募告之禁。

translations.literal: But common people sought wealth and repaid grudges; lawsuits became troublesome and disturbing; before long, the prohibition on recruiting informants was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners soon used the reward to settle scores and enrich themselves, flooding the courts with suits, and before long the informant bounty was abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，茶鹽榷酤課額少者，募豪民主之。

translations.literal: Earlier, where the quota for tea, salt, and monopoly liquor was small, powerful local families were recruited to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, where tea, salt, and liquor monopoly quotas were low, wealthy locals were recruited to run the franchises.

sentences.zh: 民多增額求利，歲更荒儉，商旅不行，至虧常課，乃籍其資產以償。

translations.literal: The people often increased the quota to seek profit; years alternated between famine and scarcity; merchants and travelers did not travel; they even fell short of the regular levy, and then their assets were registered to make repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Contractors often raised quotas to maximize profit. In bad harvest years trade collapsed, regular revenue fell short, and their assets were seized to cover the loss.

sentences.zh: 太宗始詔以開寶八年為額，既又慮其未均，乃遣使分詣諸州，同長吏裁定。

translations.literal: Taizong first decreed that the quota of Kaibao 8 be used; then, fearing it was not even, he sent envoys to the various prefectures to fix it together with the chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong first fixed quotas at the Kaibao 8 level, then, fearing uneven burdens, dispatched envoys to each prefecture to set quotas jointly with local chiefs.

sentences.zh: 凡左藏及諸庫受納諸州上供均輸金銀、絲帛暨他物，令監臨官謹視之。

translations.literal: For all goods received into the Left Treasury and the various storehouses—gold, silver, silk, and other items submitted and transported from the prefectures—supervising officials were ordered to watch carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, silk, and other tribute and transport goods accepted into the Left Treasury and other storehouses were placed under strict supervision.

sentences.zh: 欺而多取，主稱、藏吏皆斬，監臨官亦重置其罪。

translations.literal: If they deceived and took too much, the chief weighers and warehouse clerks were all beheaded, and the supervising officials also received heavy punishment for their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fraudulent over-collection was punishable by decapitation for weighers and warehouse clerks, with heavy penalties for supervising officials as well.

sentences.zh: 罷三司大將及軍將主諸州榷課，命使臣分掌。

translations.literal: The Three Departments' senior generals and military officers who managed the monopoly levies of the various prefectures were dismissed, and mission officials were ordered to take charge in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished Three Departments generals and military officers who ran prefectural monopolies and assigned imperial commissioners to take over.

sentences.zh: 掌務官吏虧課當罰，長吏以下分等連坐。

translations.literal: Officials in charge who fell short of the levy were to be punished; the chief officials and those below were jointly punished by graded ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials responsible for revenue shortfalls were punished, with graded joint liability extending down from the prefectural chief.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，令三分勾院糾本部陷失官錢，及百千賞以十之一，至五千貫者遷其職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, the Three Departments' audit offices were ordered to investigate lost official money in their departments; for amounts reaching one hundred strings, one-tenth was rewarded; for five thousand strings, office was transferred in promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2, the Three Departments' audit bureaus were ordered to pursue missing official funds in their jurisdictions: informants received one-tenth of sums recovered from one hundred strings upward, and officials who recovered five thousand strings were promoted.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年詔曰：“周設司會之職，以一歲為準；

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua an edict said: 'Zhou established the office of Grand Accountant, taking one year as the standard;
translations.idiomatic: An edict of Chunhua 1 read: "Zhou established the office of Grand Accountant on an annual standard;

sentences.zh: 漢製上計之法，以三年為期。

translations.literal: Han instituted the method of submitting accounts upward, with three years as the term.
translations.idiomatic: Han devised the upward accounting system on a three-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 所以詳知國用之盈虛，大行群吏之誅賞，斯乃舊典，其可廢乎？

translations.literal: By this one may know in detail the surplus and deficit of state expenditure, and broadly carry out punishment and reward for the host of officials—this is the old canon; how can it be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Thereby to track the state's surplus and deficit and to reward or punish officials at scale. Such was the ancient practice—can it be abandoned?

sentences.zh: 三司自今每歲具見管金銀、錢帛、軍儲等簿以聞。

translations.literal: From now the Three Departments shall each year compile registers of gold, silver, cash, silk, military stores, and the like under their charge and report them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Three Departments shall submit annual registers of gold, silver, cash, silk, military stores, and related holdings.

sentences.zh: ”四年，改三司為總計司，左右大計分掌十道財賦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Three Departments were changed to the General Accounts Office; the Left and Right Grand Accountants divided control of the fiscal revenues of the ten circuits.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year the Three Departments became the General Accounts Office, with Left and Right Grand Accountants each overseeing the finances of five circuits.

sentences.zh: 令京東西南北各以五十州為率，每州軍歲計金銀、錢、繒帛、芻粟等費，逐路關報總計司，總計司置簿，左右計使通計置裁給，餘州亦如之。

translations.literal: It was ordered that east, west, south, and north of the capital each take fifty prefectures as the standard; each prefecture and army district was to calculate yearly the costs of gold, silver, cash, silk, fodder, grain, and the like; each circuit was to report to the General Accounts Office; the General Accounts Office kept registers; the Left and Right Accountants jointly calculated and set allocations; the remaining prefectures were treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four capital circuits was to take fifty prefectures as a unit. Every prefecture and army district was to report annual expenditures in gold, silver, cash, silk, fodder, and grain to its circuit, which forwarded them to the General Accounts Office. The Left and Right Accountants then calculated allocations; other prefectures followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為三部。

translations.literal: Before long, it was restored to three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the office reverted to the three-department form.

sentences.zh: 宋聚兵京師，外州無留財，天下支用悉出三司，故其費浸多。

translations.literal: The Song concentrated troops in the capital; the outer prefectures retained no funds; all expenditure under Heaven came from the Three Departments, so their costs gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Song concentrated armies in the capital and allowed no funds to remain in the provinces, virtually all imperial expenditure passed through the Three Departments, and their costs steadily rose.

sentences.zh: 太宗孜孜庶務，或親為裁決。

translations.literal: Taizong was diligent in the myriad affairs of government and sometimes personally made decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong attended diligently to administration and sometimes decided fiscal matters in person.

sentences.zh: 有司嚐言油衣、帟幕損破者數萬段，帝令煮之，染以雜色，製旗幟數千。

translations.literal: The responsible offices once reported that tens of thousands of sections of oiled garments and tent curtains were damaged; the emperor ordered them boiled, dyed in mixed colors, and made into several thousand banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported tens of thousands of damaged oiled coats and tent panels, the emperor had them boiled, dyed in mixed colors, and turned into several thousand banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 調退材給窯務為薪，俾擇其可用者造什物數千事。

translations.literal: Reclaimed timber was allocated to the kiln offices as fuel, and they were made to select what could be used to make several thousand assorted items.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus lumber was sent to the imperial kilns as fuel, and usable pieces were fashioned into thousands of assorted goods.

sentences.zh: 其愛民惜費類此。

translations.literal: His love for the people and sparing of expense were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His frugality and care for the people took such forms.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，詔三司經度茶、鹽、酒稅以充歲用，勿增賦斂以困黎元。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, he decreed that the Three Departments plan tea, salt, and liquor taxes to meet yearly use, and not increase levies and exactions to distress the common people.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding to the throne, Zhenzong ordered the Three Departments to manage tea, salt, and liquor taxes for annual needs and not to increase levies that would burden the people.

sentences.zh: 是時條禁愈密，較課以租額前界遞年相參。

translations.literal: At this time regulations and prohibitions grew stricter; revenue was compared using the rent quota of the previous term and successive years in mutual reference.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations grew tighter, and revenue targets were assessed against prior quotas and year-by-year comparisons.

sentences.zh: 景德初，榷務連歲增羨，三司即取多收者為額。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, monopoly offices for several years increased their surplus; the Three Departments immediately took the higher collections as the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, as monopoly revenues rose several years in a row, the Three Departments promptly set quotas at the highest collected level.

sentences.zh: 帝慮或致掊克，詔凡增額比奏。

translations.literal: The emperor feared this might lead to extortion; he decreed that all quota increases must be reported for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing extortion, the emperor required every quota increase to be reported for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 上封者言：“諸路歲課增羨，知州、通判皆書曆為課最，有虧者則無罰。

translations.literal: A memorial presenter said: 'When yearly levies on the various circuits increased in surplus, the prefects and general assessors all recorded it in their calendars as top performance; if there was a deficit, there was no punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: A memorialist said: "When circuit revenues exceeded quota, prefects and general assessors recorded the surplus as outstanding performance, but shortfalls went unpunished.

sentences.zh: ”乃令諸路茶、鹽、酒稅及諸場務，自今總一歲之課，合為一，以額較之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was ordered that on the various circuits tea, salt, liquor taxes, and the various field offices from now on total one year's levy, combine them into one, and compare them to the quota.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered that tea, salt, liquor taxes, and all field offices on each circuit combine their annual receipts into a single total for comparison with the quota.

sentences.zh: 有虧則計分數，知州、通判減監官一等科罰，州司典吏減專典一等論，大臣及武臣知州軍者止罰通判以下。

translations.literal: If there was a deficit, the fractional shortfall was calculated; prefects and general assessors were punished one grade below supervising officials; prefectural clerks and record keepers were punished one grade below specialist clerks; great ministers and military officials serving as prefects were punished only from the general assessor downward.
translations.idiomatic: Deficits were measured in proportional points. Prefects and general assessors were penalized one grade below supervising officials; prefectural clerks one grade below specialists. Where a grand minister or military man served as prefect, only the general assessor and subordinates were punished.

sentences.zh: 至道末，天下總入緡錢二千二百二十四萬五千八百。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhidao, total revenue under Heaven in strings of cash was 22,245,800.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhidao era, total empire-wide revenue in cash strings was 22,245,800.

sentences.zh: 三歲一親祀郊丘，計緡錢常五百餘萬，大半以金銀、綾綺、絁綢平其直給之。

translations.literal: Every three years the emperor personally sacrificed at the suburban altar; the calculated strings of cash were regularly more than five million; the greater part was paid by balancing value with gold, silver, damask, silk gauze, and coarse silk.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice, costing routinely more than five million strings of cash, mostly paid in gold, silver, and silks at assessed value.

sentences.zh: 天禧末，上供惟錢帛增多，餘以移用頗減舊數，而天下總入一萬五千八十五萬一百，出一萬二千六百七十七萬五千二百，而贏數不預焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianxi, tribute upward in cash and silk alone increased; other items transferred for use were considerably reduced from old figures; yet total revenue under Heaven was 150,850,100, expenditure 126,775,200, and surplus figures were not included.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tianxi, only cash and silk tribute had risen sharply, while other categories transferred for use fell well below earlier levels. Total revenue reached 150,850,100 strings, expenditure 126,775,200, not counting surpluses.

sentences.zh: 景德郊祀七百餘萬，東封八百餘萬，祀汾陰、上寶冊又增二十萬。

translations.literal: The Jingde suburban sacrifice cost more than seven million; the eastern feng cost more than eight million; sacrifice at Fenyin and presentation of the precious register added another two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingde suburban rite cost over seven million; the eastern feng over eight million; the Fenyin sacrifice and presentation of the precious register added another two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 丁謂為三司使，著《景德會計錄》以獻，林特領使，亦繼為之。

translations.literal: Ding Wei served as Three Departments commissioner, compiled the 《Jingde Accounting Records》 and presented them; Lin Te led the office and also succeeded in doing so.
translations.idiomatic: As Three Departments commissioner, Ding Wei compiled and presented the 《Jingde Accounting Records》; Lin Te, who succeeded him as commissioner, did the same.

sentences.zh: 凡舉大禮，有司皆籍當時所費以聞，必優詔獎之。

translations.literal: Whenever great rites were performed, the responsible offices all recorded the costs at the time and reported them; an edict of special praise was invariably issued.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a major rite was held, officials recorded its costs and reported them, and the emperor invariably issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 初，吳、蜀、江南、荊湖、南粵皆號富強，相繼降附，太祖、太宗因其蓄藏，守以恭儉簡易。

translations.literal: At first Wu, Shu, Jiangnan, Jinghu, and southern Yue were all called rich and strong; they submitted in succession; Taizu and Taizong relied on their accumulated stores and maintained respectful frugality and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wu, Shu, Jiangnan, Jinghu, and southern Yue were all renowned for wealth. After they submitted in turn, Taizu and Taizong drew on their accumulated stores while governing with respectful frugality.

sentences.zh: 天下生齒尚寡，而養兵未甚蕃，任官未甚冗，佛老之徒未甚熾；

translations.literal: The population under Heaven was still few; maintaining troops was not very extensive; appointing officials was not very redundant; followers of Buddhism and Daoism were not very flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: The population was still small, the army not yet very large, the bureaucracy not yet bloated, and Buddhist and Daoist establishments not yet dominant;

sentences.zh: 外無金繒之遺，百姓亦各安其生，不為巧偽放侈，故上下給足，府庫羨溢。

translations.literal: abroad there was no legacy of gold and silk; the common people each rested in their livelihoods and did not practice craft, fraud, or extravagant release; therefore above and below were supplied in full, and the treasuries overflowed with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: no great foreign drain on treasure existed, and the people lived securely without fraud or extravagance. Supply met demand at every level, and the treasuries brimmed with surplus.

sentences.zh: 承平既久，戶口歲增，兵籍益廣，吏員益眾。

translations.literal: After long peace, household registers increased year by year, military registers grew broader, and official posts grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged peace, population, military rolls, and the civil service all expanded year by year.

sentences.zh: 佛老、外國耗蠹中土，縣官之費數倍於昔，百姓亦稍縱侈，而上下始困於財矣。

translations.literal: Buddhism, Daoism, and foreign states drained and harmed the central land; state expenditure was several times that of old; the common people also slightly gave way to extravagance; and above and below began to be distressed in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Daoist institutions and foreign relations drained the empire; state costs rose severalfold over earlier times; the people grew somewhat extravagant—and court and country alike began to feel fiscal strain.

sentences.zh: 仁宗承之，經費浸廣。

translations.literal: Renzong inherited this; routine expenses gradually broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong inherited this situation, and routine expenditure steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，首命有司取景德一歲用度，較天禧所出，省其不急者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, he first ordered the responsible offices to take one year's expenditure of Jingde, compare it with Tianxi outlays, and reduce what was not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiansheng he first ordered officials to compare Jingde annual spending with Tianxi outlays and cut nonessential items.

sentences.zh: 自祥符天書一出，齋醮糜費甚眾，京城之內，一夕數處，至是，始大裁損。

translations.literal: From the time the Xiangfu Heavenly Writ appeared, fasting and offerings wasted much; within the capital, several sites in one night—to this point, large cuts were first made.
translations.idiomatic: Since the appearance of the Xiangfu Heavenly Writ, fasting rites had consumed vast sums, with several sites active in the capital on a single night. Now these were sharply reduced for the first time.

sentences.zh: 京師營造，多內侍傳旨呼索，費無藝極。

translations.literal: Construction in the capital was largely by inner attendants transmitting edicts to summon and demand; costs had no limit of art.
translations.idiomatic: Capital construction was often ordered by palace eunuchs summoning materials on imperial authority, with costs bound by no rule.

sentences.zh: 帝與太后知其弊，詔自今營造所須，先下三司度功費然後給。

translations.literal: The emperor and the empress dowager knew these abuses; they decreed that from now on whatever construction required must first be sent to the Three Departments to estimate labor and cost, and only then be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress dowager recognized the abuse and decreed that henceforth all construction needs must be estimated by the Three Departments before funds were issued.

sentences.zh: 又減內外宮觀清衛卒及工匠，分隸諸軍、八作司。

translations.literal: They also reduced the purifying guard soldiers and artisans of inner and outer palaces and monasteries, assigning them in divisions to the various armies and the Eight Works Office.
translations.idiomatic: They also cut guard soldiers and artisans attached to palace and temple establishments, reassigning them to regular armies and the Eight Works Office.

sentences.zh: 舊殿直已上，雖幼未任朝謁，遇乾元、長寧節皆賜服，至是亦罷給。

translations.literal: By old custom, those of Palace Duty rank and above, though young and not yet attending court audiences, on Qiankun and Changning festivals were all granted garments; at this point that grant was also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By former custom, even junior palace attendants too young for court audiences received festival garments on Qiankun and Changning days; these grants were now abolished.

sentences.zh: 故事，上尊號、諡號，隨冊寶物並用黃金。

translations.literal: By precedent, when bestowing honorific titles and posthumous titles, the accompanying register and treasure objects all used gold.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, honorific and posthumous titles were accompanied by register and treasure objects made of solid gold.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“先帝、太后用黃金，若朕所禦，止用塗金。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The former emperor and empress dowager used gold; for what concerns me, only gilding is to be used.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "My predecessors used solid gold; for my own regalia, gilding alone will suffice.

sentences.zh: ”時洞真宮、壽寧觀相繼災，宰相張知白請罷不急營造，以答天戒。

translations.literal: At that time the Dongzhen Palace and Shouning Abbey suffered fire in succession; the chief councilor Zhang Zhibai requested that nonurgent construction be stopped to answer Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: " When fires struck the Dongzhen Palace and Shouning Abbey in succession, Chief Councilor Zhang Zhibai asked to halt nonessential construction in response to Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 及滑州塞決河，御史知雜王鬷復以為言。

translations.literal: When Huazhou blocked a breached river, the supervising censor Wang Zong again spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the breach at Huazhou was sealed, Supervising Censor Wang Zong raised the same plea.

sentences.zh: 既而玉清昭應宮災，遂詔諭中外，不復繕修。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Yujing Zhaoying Palace burned; thereupon an edict was issued informing inner and outer circles that it would not be repaired again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yujing Zhaoying Palace burned, an edict announced to the empire that it would not be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 自是道家之奉有節，土木之費省矣。

translations.literal: From this, Daoist offerings had moderation, and costs for earth and timber were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist state patronage was thereafter restrained, and construction costs fell.

sentences.zh: 帝天資恭儉，尤務約己以先天下，有司言利者，多擯不取。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature respectful and frugal, especially devoted to restraining himself first to lead all under Heaven; when offices spoke of profit, he mostly rejected and did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was naturally modest and frugal, leading by personal restraint. Proposals aimed chiefly at profit were usually rejected.

sentences.zh: 聞民之有疾苦，雖厚利，舍之無所愛。

translations.literal: When he heard that the people had suffering and hardship, even great profit he abandoned without regret.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the people suffered hardship, he would abandon even lucrative revenue without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 貢獻珍異，故事有者，或罷之。

translations.literal: Tribute of rare and precious objects—where precedent existed, some were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Some exotic tribute items required by precedent were abolished.

sentences.zh: 山林、川澤、陂池之利，久與民共者，屢敕有司毋輒禁止。

translations.literal: The benefits of mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, and ponds long shared with the people—he repeatedly decreed that the responsible offices must not lightly forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly ordered officials not to prohibit access to mountains, rivers, marshes, and ponds long shared with the people.

sentences.zh: 至於州縣征取苛細，蠲減蓋不可勝數。

translations.literal: As for harsh and minute exactions by prefectures and counties, remissions and reductions were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh or petty levies by prefectures and counties were remitted in countless instances.

sentences.zh: 至寶元中，陝西用兵，調度百出，縣官之費益廣。

translations.literal: By Baoyuan, war was waged in Shaanxi; arrangements for supplies issued in a hundred ways; state expenditure grew broader still.
translations.idiomatic: By Baoyuan, war in Shaanxi multiplied supply arrangements, and state costs grew still further.

sentences.zh: 天章閣侍讀賈昌朝言：“臣嚐治畿邑，邑有禁兵三千，而留萬戶賦輸，僅能取足，郊祀慶賞，乃出自內府。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy reader Jia Changchao said: 'Your servant once governed a capital district county; the county had three thousand forbidden troops, yet retained the tax deliveries of ten thousand households and could barely make ends meet; suburban sacrifice rewards came from the inner treasury.'
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin reader Jia Changchao said: "I once governed a capital-region county. It had three thousand garrison troops but only the tax yield of ten thousand households, barely enough to meet obligations; suburban rewards came from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 計江、淮歲運糧六百餘萬石，以一歲之入，僅能充期月之用，三分二在軍旅，一在冗食，先所蓄聚，不盈數載。

translations.literal: It is calculated that the Jiang and Huai yearly transport of grain is more than six million piculs; with one year's income, it can barely fill one month's use; two-thirds go to the army, one-third to redundant consumption; what was formerly stored does not fill several years.'
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai grain transport exceeds six million piculs a year, yet annual revenue barely covers one month's spending: two-thirds goes to the military, one-third to waste. Stored reserves would not last several years.

sentences.zh: 天下久無事，而財不藏於國，又不在民，儻有水旱軍戎之急，計將安出？

translations.literal: The realm has long been without trouble, yet wealth is stored neither in the state nor among the people; if there should be urgent need from flood, drought, or military campaign, from what plan will it come forth?'
translations.idiomatic: The empire has been at peace for years, yet wealth sits neither in the treasury nor with the people. If flood, drought, or war strikes, where will funds come from?

sentences.zh: ”於是議省冗費。

translations.literal: Thereupon discussion turned to reducing redundant expense.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then debated cutting waste.

sentences.zh: 右司諫韓琦言：“省費當自掖庭始。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Han Qi said: 'Saving expense should begin with the inner palace.'
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrator Han Qi said: "Economy should begin in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 請詔三司取先朝及近歲賜予日費之數，裁為中製，無名者一切罷之。

translations.literal: I request that an edict order the Three Departments to take the numbers of daily grants and gifts of former courts and recent years, trim them to a moderate standard, and abolish all that have no proper name.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Three Departments review daily grants and gifts of earlier reigns and recent years, set a moderate standard, and abolish all unnamed items.

sentences.zh: ”乃令入內內侍省、禦藥院、內東門司裁定，有司不預焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Inner Palace Directorate, Imperial Pharmacy, and Inner East Gate Office were ordered to fix the amounts; the regular offices did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: " The Inner Palace Directorate, Imperial Pharmacy, and Inner East Gate Office were ordered to set the amounts without regular agencies taking part.

sentences.zh: 議者或欲損吏兵奉賜。

translations.literal: Some in the discussion wished to reduce the salaries and grants of officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed cutting official and military salaries and allowances.

sentences.zh: 帝謂：“祿廩皆有定制，毋遽變更以搖人心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Salaries and grain rations all have fixed regulations; do not hastily change them to shake people's hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Salaries and rations are fixed by regulation; do not change them hastily and unsettle morale.

sentences.zh: ”尹洙在陝西，請為鬻爵之法，亦不果行。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu in Shaanxi requested a law for selling ranks; this also did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu in Shaanxi proposed selling offices for revenue, but that too was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 其後西兵久不解，財用益屈，內出詔書：“減皇后至宗室婦郊祠半賜，著為式；

translations.literal: Later the western campaign long went unresolved; finances grew more strained; an edict issued from within said: 'Reduce by half the suburban sacrifice grants from the empress down to clanswomen; establish this as a rule;
translations.idiomatic: As the western war dragged on and finances tightened, an inner edict declared: "Halve suburban grants to the empress and clanswomen, and make this permanent rule;

sentences.zh: 皇后、嬪禦進奉乾元節回賜物皆減半，宗室、外命婦回賜權罷。

translations.literal: the empress, consorts, and imperial ladies' offerings and return gifts for the Qiankun festival are all halved; return gifts to the imperial clan and women of outside appointment are provisionally suspended.'
translations.idiomatic: halve Qiankun festival gifts to the empress and consorts; suspend return gifts to the imperial clan and titled ladies.

sentences.zh: ”於是皇后、嬪禦各上奉錢五月以助軍費，宗室刺史已上，亦納公使錢之半。

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress, consorts, and imperial ladies each presented tribute money for five months to aid military costs; imperial clansmen of prefect rank and above also paid half their public-service money.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress and consorts then each contributed five months' stipends to military funds, and imperial clansmen of prefect rank and above paid half their public-service allowances.

sentences.zh: 荊王元儼盡納公使錢，詔給其半，後以元儼叔父，全給如故。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Yuan Yan paid all his public-service money; an edict granted him half back; later, because Yuan Yan was the emperor's uncle, the full grant was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Yuan Yan paid his full public-service allowance; the court returned half, then restored the full amount because he was the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 帝亦命罷左藏庫月進錢一千二百緡。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered abolished the Left Treasury's monthly advance of 1,200 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also abolished the Left Treasury's monthly advance of 1,200 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 公卿、近臣以次減郊祠所賜銀絹，舊四千、三千者損一千，千損三百，三百損百，百損二十，皆著為式。

translations.literal: Grand ministers and close officials in order had their suburban sacrifice gifts of silver and silk reduced: former four thousand and three thousand were cut by one thousand; one thousand by three hundred; three hundred by one hundred; one hundred by twenty—all established as rules.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers and close officials had suburban gifts of silver and silk reduced stepwise: former grants of four or three thousand were cut by one thousand; one thousand by three hundred; three hundred by one hundred; one hundred by twenty—all codified as permanent rules.

sentences.zh: 三司使王堯臣取陝西、河北、河東三路未用兵及用兵後歲出入財用之數，會計以聞。

translations.literal: Three Departments commissioner Wang Yao-chen took the yearly revenue and expenditure figures of Shaanxi, Hebei, and Hedong circuits before and after military use, compiled accounts, and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments commissioner Wang Yao-chen compiled and reported annual revenue and expenditure for the Shaanxi, Hebei, and Hedong circuits before and after the war.

sentences.zh: 寶元元年未用兵，三路出入錢帛糧草：陝西入一千九百七十八萬，出二千一百五十一萬；

translations.literal: In Baoyuan 1, before military use, the three circuits' revenue and expenditure in cash, silk, grain, and fodder: Shaanxi revenue 19,780,000, expenditure 21,510,000;
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyuan 1, before hostilities, the three circuits' cash, silk, grain, and fodder accounts were: Shaanxi, revenue 19,780,000, expenditure 21,510,000;

sentences.zh: 河北入二千一十四萬，出一千八百二十三萬；

translations.literal: Hebei revenue 20,140,000, expenditure 18,230,000;
translations.idiomatic: Hebei, revenue 20,140,000, expenditure 18,230,000;

sentences.zh: 河東入一千三十八萬，出八百五十九萬。

translations.literal: Hedong revenue 10,380,000, expenditure 8,590,000.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, revenue 10,380,000, expenditure 8,590,000.

sentences.zh: 用兵後，陝西入三千三百九十萬，出三千三百六十三萬，蓋視河東、北尤劇，以兵屯陝西特多故也。

translations.literal: After military use, Shaanxi revenue 33,900,000, expenditure 33,630,000—this was especially severe compared with Hedong and Hebei, because troops stationed in Shaanxi were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After hostilities, Shaanxi revenue was 33,900,000 and expenditure 33,630,000—far heavier than Hedong or Hebei because troops were concentrated there in greatest number.

sentences.zh: 又計京師出入金帛：寶元元年，入一千九百五十萬，出二千一百八十五萬，是歲郊祠，故出入之數視常歲為多；

translations.literal: He also calculated the capital's revenue and expenditure in gold and silk: Baoyuan 1, revenue 19,500,000, expenditure 21,850,000—this year had the suburban sacrifice, so the revenue and expenditure figures were greater than a normal year;
translations.idiomatic: Capital gold and silk accounts were also compiled: in Baoyuan 1, revenue 19,500,000 and expenditure 21,850,000—the higher figures reflected that year's suburban sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，入二千九百二十九萬，出二千六百一十七萬，而奇數皆不預焉。

translations.literal: Qingli 2, revenue 29,290,000, expenditure 26,170,000—and odd amounts were not included.
translations.idiomatic: in Qingli 2, revenue 29,290,000 and expenditure 26,170,000, not counting miscellaneous items.

sentences.zh: 會元昊請臣，朝廷亦已厭兵，屈意撫納，歲賜繒、茶增至二十五萬；

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao requested to become a subject, the court had also grown weary of war and bent its intent to soothe and accept him; yearly gifts of silk and tea increased to 250,000;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao submitted, the court, weary of war, conciliated him and raised annual gifts of silk and tea to 250,000;

sentences.zh: 而契丹邀割地，復增歲遺至五十萬，自是歲費彌有所加。

translations.literal: but the Khitan demanded ceded territory and again increased the yearly gift to 500,000; from this yearly costs further increased.
translations.idiomatic: but the Khitan demanded territory and raised the annual tribute to 500,000, and yearly costs rose still further.

sentences.zh: 西兵既罷，而調用無所減，乃下詔切責邊臣及轉運司趣議裁節，稍徙戍兵還內地。

translations.literal: After the western campaign ended, allocations were not reduced; thereupon an edict sternly reproached frontier officials and transport commissioners to hurry discussion of cuts and savings, and gradually moved garrison troops back to the inner regions.
translations.idiomatic: When the western war ended, military spending did not fall. The emperor issued a stern edict ordering frontier officials and transport commissioners to propose cuts and gradually moved garrison troops back to the interior.

sentences.zh: 命三司戶部副使包拯行河北，與邊臣、轉運司議罷省冗官，汰軍士之不任役者。

translations.literal: It was ordered that Three Departments Vice Commissioner for Households Bao Zheng travel Hebei and, with frontier officials and transport commissioners, discuss abolishing redundant officials and eliminating soldiers unfit for service.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Bao Zheng, vice commissioner of the Three Departments' Households Bureau, to tour Hebei and, with frontier officials and transport commissioners, discuss cutting redundant officials and dismissing soldiers unfit for duty.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士承旨王堯臣等較近歲天下財賦出入之數，相參耗登。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin Academician Expositor Wang Yao-chen and others to compare recent years' figures for revenue and expenditure under Heaven, mutually referring surplus and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hanlin expositor Wang Yao-chen and others to compare recent empire-wide revenue and expenditure and reconcile surpluses and deficits.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年，入一億二千六百二十五萬一千九百六十四，而所出無餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangyou, revenue was 126,251,964, and expenditure left nothing remaining.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 1, revenue reached 126,251,964, with nothing left after expenditure.

sentences.zh: 堯臣等為書七卷上之，送三司，取一歲中數以為定式。

translations.literal: Wang Yao-chen and others compiled a work in seven scrolls and presented it upward; it was sent to the Three Departments to take one year's figures as the fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yao-chen and his colleagues compiled a seven-scroll report, sent it to the Three Departments, and established one year's figures as the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗時，內外兵九十一萬二千，宗室、吏員受祿者九千七百八十五。

translations.literal: At first, in Zhenzong's time, inner and outer troops numbered 912,000; clansmen and officials receiving salaries numbered 9,785.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong, inner and outer forces totaled 912,000 men, and clansmen and salaried officials numbered 9,785.

sentences.zh: 寶元以後，募兵益廣，宗室蕃衍，吏員歲增。

translations.literal: After Baoyuan, recruited troops grew broader; the imperial clan proliferated; officials increased year by year.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyuan, recruitment expanded, the imperial clan grew, and the bureaucracy increased yearly.

sentences.zh: 至是，兵一百二十五萬九千，宗室、吏員受祿者萬五千四百四十三，祿廩奉賜從而增廣。

translations.literal: By this point, troops numbered 1,259,000; clansmen and officials receiving salaries numbered 15,443; salaries, grain rations, and grants broadened accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: By then troops numbered 1,259,000 and salaried clansmen and officials 15,443, with salaries, rations, and allowances rising accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及景德中，祀南郊，內外賞賚金帛、緡錢總六百一萬。

translations.literal: In the Jingde period, when sacrificing at the southern suburb, inner and outer rewards in gold, silk, and strings of cash totaled 6,010,000.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingde southern suburban sacrifice, inner and outer rewards in gold, silk, and cash totaled 6,010,000.

sentences.zh: 至是，饗明堂，增至一千二百餘萬，故用度不得不屈。

translations.literal: By this point, when feasting at the Bright Hall, the amount increased to more than 12,000,000; therefore expenditure could not but be constrained.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Bright Hall feast cost over twelve million, forcing expenditure to be squeezed.

sentences.zh: 至和中，諫官範鎮上疏曰：“陛下每遇水旱之災，必露立仰天，痛自刻責，而吏不稱職，陛下憂勤於上，人民愁歎於下。

translations.literal: In the Zhihe period, Remonstrator Fan Zhen memorialized, saying: 'Whenever Your Majesty meets flood or drought disasters, you stand exposed beneath the sky, looking upward, and painfully blame yourself; yet officials do not fulfill their posts, while Your Majesty toils in concern above and the people groan in sorrow below.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhihe, Remonstrator Fan Zhen memorialized: "Whenever flood or drought strikes, Your Majesty stands in the open air, looking heavenward in self-reproach, while officials fail in their duties. You toil in concern above as the people groan below.

sentences.zh: 今歲無麥，朝廷為放稅免役及發倉廩拯貸，存恤之恩不為不至。

translations.literal: This year there is no wheat; the court has remitted taxes, exempted corvée, and opened granaries for relief loans—the grace of preservation and comfort is not less than complete.
translations.idiomatic: This year the wheat crop has failed. The court has remitted taxes, exempted corvée, and opened granaries for relief loans—mercy could hardly be more complete.

sentences.zh: 然人民流離，父母妻子不相保者，平居無事時，不少寬其力役，輕其租賦；

translations.literal: Yet the people are displaced; fathers, mothers, wives, and children cannot keep one another safe—in ordinary peaceful times, their labor and corvée are not much lightened, nor their rent and tax much reduced;
translations.idiomatic: Yet people still flee their homes, unable to keep families together. Even in peaceful times their corvée is not lightened nor their taxes reduced;

sentences.zh: 歲大熟，民不得終歲之飽；

translations.literal: in years of great harvest, the people cannot obtain a full year's satiety;
translations.idiomatic: in bumper years they cannot eat their fill for a whole year;

sentences.zh: 及有小歉，雖加重放，已不及事。

translations.literal: when there is a small shortfall, even if heavier remissions are added, it is already too late for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: and when harvests fail, even heavier remissions come too late.

sentences.zh: 此無他，重斂之政在前也。

translations.literal: This has no other cause: heavy exaction policies came before.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is simple: heavy exactions came first.

sentences.zh: 國家自陝西用兵以來，賦役煩重。

translations.literal: Since the state waged war in Shaanxi, levies and corvée have been burdensome and numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shaanxi war, levies and corvée have multiplied.

sentences.zh: 及近年，轉運使復於常賦外進羨錢以助南郊，其餘無名斂率不可勝計。

translations.literal: In recent years, transport commissioners again presented surplus money beyond the regular levy to assist the southern suburban sacrifice; other nameless exactions and rates are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years transport commissioners again submitted surplus funds beyond regular levies to help fund the southern suburban rite, while countless other unnamed exactions piled on.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 又言：“古者塚宰製國用，今中書主民，樞密主兵，三司主財，各不相知。

translations.literal: He also said: 'In antiquity the Grand Steward regulated state expenditure; today the Secretariat governs the people, the Bureau of Military Affairs governs troops, and the Three Departments govern wealth—each does not know the others.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In antiquity the Grand Steward regulated state expenditure. Today the Secretariat governs the people, the Bureau of Military Affairs the army, and the Three Departments wealth—each in ignorance of the others.

sentences.zh: 故財已匱而樞密院益兵不已，民已困而三司取財不已。

translations.literal: Thus when wealth is already exhausted, the Bureau of Military Affairs still increases troops without cease; when the people are already distressed, the Three Departments still take wealth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury funds are exhausted, yet the Bureau of Military Affairs keeps enlarging the army; the people are exhausted, yet the Three Departments keep extracting revenue.

sentences.zh: 中書視民之困，而不知使樞密減兵、三司寬財者，製國用之職不在中書也。

translations.literal: The Secretariat sees the people's distress yet does not know how to make the Bureau of Military Affairs reduce troops or the Three Departments ease wealth—because the duty of regulating state expenditure is not in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat sees popular distress but cannot order troop cuts or fiscal relief because regulating state expenditure is not its charge.

sentences.zh: 願使中書、樞密通知兵民財利大計，與三司量其出入，製為國用，則天下民力庶幾少寬。

translations.literal: I wish that the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs be informed of the great plan for troops, people, wealth, and profit, and together with the Three Departments measure revenue and expenditure and regulate state use—then the people's strength under Heaven might somewhat be eased.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs coordinate with the Three Departments on troops, people, and revenue, and set national expenditure accordingly—the people's burden might then ease somewhat.

sentences.zh: ”然自天聖以來，帝以經費為慮，屢命官裁節，而有司不能承上之意，卒無所建明。

translations.literal: Yet from Tiansheng onward, the emperor, concerned about routine expenses, repeatedly ordered officials to cut and save, but the responsible offices could not carry out the emperor's intent and in the end proposed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Tiansheng onward, though the emperor repeatedly ordered economies, the agencies failed to carry out his intent and proposed nothing effective.

sentences.zh: 治平中，兵數少損，隸籍者猶百十六萬二千，宗室、吏員視皇祐無慮增十之三。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping period, troop numbers were somewhat reduced; those on the registers still numbered 1,162,000; clansmen and officials compared with Huangyou increased by no less than three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping troop numbers fell somewhat, but registered forces still totaled 1,162,000, while clansmen and officials rose at least thirty percent over Huangyou levels.

sentences.zh: 英宗以勤儉自飭，然享國日淺，於經紀法度所未暇焉。

translations.literal: Yingzong restrained himself with diligence and frugality, yet his reign was brief and he had no leisure for organizing laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong practiced diligence and frugality, but his reign was brief and he had no time to reorganize fiscal institutions.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，內外入一億一千六百十三萬八千四百五，出一億二千三十四萬三千一百七十四，非常出者又一千一百五十二萬一千二百七十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, inner and outer revenue was 116,138,405, expenditure 120,343,174, and extraordinary expenditure another 11,521,278.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping 2, revenue was 116,138,405 and regular expenditure 120,343,174, with another 11,521,278 in extraordinary spending.

sentences.zh: 是歲，諸路積一億六千二十九萬二千九十三，而京師不預焉。

translations.literal: That year, the various circuits accumulated 160,292,093, not counting the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year the circuits held reserves of 160,292,093, excluding the capital.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，尤先理財。

translations.literal: When Shenzong succeeded to the throne, he especially put managing wealth first.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding to the throne, Shenzong made fiscal management a top priority.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，命翰林學士司馬光等置局看詳裁減國用制度，仍取慶曆二年數，比今支費不同者，開析以聞。

translations.literal: Early in Xining, he ordered Hanlin Academician Sima Guang and others to establish a bureau to examine and reduce institutions of state expenditure, still taking the figures of Qingli 2, opening and analyzing where present expenditure differed, and reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining he ordered Sima Guang and others to establish a bureau to review and cut state spending, comparing current costs with Qingli 2 figures and reporting discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 後數日，光登對言：“國用不足，在用度大奢，賞賜不節，宗室繁多，官職冗濫，軍旅不精。

translations.literal: Several days later, Guang answered in audience, saying: 'State revenue is insufficient because expenditure is greatly extravagant, rewards are uncontrolled, the imperial clan is numerous, offices are redundantly numerous, and the army is not refined.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Guang told the emperor in audience: "Revenue is short because spending is extravagant, rewards uncontrolled, the imperial clan large, offices redundant, and the army inefficient.

sentences.zh: 必須陛下與兩府大臣及三司官吏，深思救弊之術，磨以歲月，庶幾有效，非愚臣一朝一夕所能裁減。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must, together with the two palace ministers and Three Departments officials, deeply consider methods to rescue abuses and grind away at them over months and years—then there may be some effect. It is not what your foolish servant can reduce in a morning and evening.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must work with the chief ministers and Three Departments over months and years on real reforms. This cannot be fixed overnight by one official.

sentences.zh: ”帝遂罷裁減局，但下三司共析。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon abolished the reduction bureau but only ordered the Three Departments jointly to analyze.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dissolved the reduction bureau and ordered only a joint Three Departments review.

sentences.zh: 王安石執政，議置三司條例司，講修錢穀之法。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, he proposed establishing the Three Departments Regulations Office to discuss and revise methods for money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi took power, he proposed a Three Departments Regulations Office to reform fiscal administration.

sentences.zh: 帝因論措置之宜，言：“今財賦非不多，但用不節，何由給足？

translations.literal: The emperor, discussing measures of arrangement, said: 'Today's wealth is not scant, but use is uncontrolled—how can supply be sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Discussing policy, the emperor said: "Wealth is not scarce, but spending is uncontrolled—how can revenue suffice?

sentences.zh: 宮中一私身之奉有及八十千者，嫁一公主至費七十萬緡，沈貴妃料錢月八百緡。

translations.literal: Within the palace, a single private person's maintenance reaches eighty thousand; marrying one princess costs as much as seven hundred thousand strings; Consort Shen's monthly allowance is eight hundred strings.'
translations.idiomatic: A single palace attendant's upkeep can reach eighty thousand cash; a princess's wedding costs seven hundred thousand strings; Consort Shen's monthly allowance is eight hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 聞太宗時宮人惟係皂綢襜，元德皇后嚐用金線緣襜，太宗怒其奢。

translations.literal: He heard that in Taizong's time palace women wore only black silk aprons; Empress Yuande once used gold thread to edge an apron, and Taizong was angry at the extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that Taizong's palace women wore only black silk aprons, and Taizong rebuked Empress Yuande for edging one with gold thread.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初定公主奉料，以問獻穆，再三始言初僅得五貫爾，異時中宮月有止七百錢者。

translations.literal: When Renzong first fixed princess allowances, he asked Xianmu, who only after repeated questioning said at first it was barely five strings; at another time an empress's monthly allowance was only seven hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong first set princess stipends, Empress Xianmu said after repeated questioning that the original amount was only five strings; at one time an empress's monthly allowance was only seven hundred cash.

sentences.zh: ”時天下承平，帝方經略四夷，故每以財用不給為憂。

translations.literal: At that time the realm enjoyed long peace, yet the emperor was planning strategy toward the four barbarians, so he often worried that revenue was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empire was at peace, the emperor was planning campaigns on the frontiers and often worried that revenue would not suffice.

sentences.zh: 日與大臣講求其故，命官考三司簿籍，商量經久廢置之宜，凡一歲用度及郊祀大費，皆編著定式。

translations.literal: Day by day he discussed the causes with great ministers, ordered officials to examine Three Departments registers, discussed measures for long-standing abolition and establishment, and compiled fixed standards for yearly expenditure and great suburban costs.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed causes daily with his ministers, ordered review of Three Departments registers, and compiled fixed standards for annual spending and major ritual costs.

sentences.zh: 有司請造龍圖、天章閣覆闌檻青氈四百九十。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested manufacture of four hundred ninety green felt coverings for the balustrades of the Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Writ halls.
translations.idiomatic: Officials requested four hundred ninety green felt balustrade covers for the Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Writ halls.

sentences.zh: 帝謂：“禁中諸殿欄檻率故弊，不必覆也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Within the forbidden precincts, the balustrades of the various halls are mostly old and worn—there is no need to cover them anew.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Palace balustrades are mostly worn already—there is no need for new covers.

sentences.zh: ”既而並延福宮覆檻氈罷之。

translations.literal: Soon after, covering felt for the balustrades of Yanfu Palace was also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, felt covers for Yanfu Palace balustrades were canceled as well.

sentences.zh: 後呂嘉問復建議省儀鸞司供禁中彩帛。

translations.literal: Later Lü Jiawen again proposed economizing on colored silks supplied by the Ceremonial Guard Office for the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Jiawen proposed cutting colored silks supplied to the inner palace by the Ceremonial Guard Office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔內外勿給土木工作，非兩宮、倉廩、武庫，皆罷省。

translations.literal: That year, an edict forbade civil and military construction work everywhere; except for the two palaces, granaries, and armories, all were stopped and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict halted construction empire-wide except for the two palaces, granaries, and armories.

sentences.zh: 三年，儀鸞司闕氈三千，三司請命河東製之。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Ceremonial Guard Office lacked three thousand felts; the Three Departments requested that Hedong manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Ceremonial Guard Office lacked three thousand felts, and the Three Departments asked Hedong to produce them.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“牛羊司積毛數萬斤，皆同糞壤，三司不取於此，而欲勤遠民乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The Cattle and Sheep Office has accumulated tens of thousands of jin of wool, all like dung and soil—the Three Departments do not take from this but wish to trouble distant people?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Cattle and Sheep Office has tens of thousands of jin of wool going to waste. Will the Three Departments trouble distant subjects rather than use it?

sentences.zh: ”金州歲貢班竹簾，簡州歲貢綿綢，安州市紅花萬斤，梓州市碌二千斤，帝皆以道遠擾民，亟命停罷。

translations.literal: Jinzhou yearly presented spotted bamboo curtains; Jianzhou yearly presented cotton silk; Anzhou presented ten thousand jin of safflower; Zizhou presented two thousand jin of indigo—all were ordered stopped because the roads were distant and the people disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute of bamboo curtains from Jinzhou, cotton silk from Jianzhou, safflower from Anzhou, and indigo from Zizhou were all halted as needlessly burdensome.

sentences.zh: 製置司言：“諸路科買上供羊，民費錢幾倍，而河北榷場博買契丹羊歲數萬，路遠，抵京皆瘦惡耗死，公私費錢四十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: The Regulatory Office said: 'On the various circuits, requisitioned tribute sheep cost the people several times the money, while the Hebei monopoly market purchased Khitan sheep by the tens of thousands yearly; the roads were long, and by the time they reached the capital all were lean, foul, and dead from loss—public and private costs in strings of cash exceeded four hundred thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: The Regulatory Office reported that circuit requisitions for tribute sheep cost the people several times the market price, while Hebei monopoly purchases of Khitan sheep—many dying en route—cost public and private funds over four hundred thousand strings yearly.

sentences.zh: ”詔著作佐郎程博文訪利害。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Editorial Assistant Cheng Bowen to investigate advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Editorial Assistant Cheng Bowen to investigate the costs and benefits.

sentences.zh: 博文募民有保任者，以產為抵，官預給錢，約期限、口數、斤重以輸。

translations.literal: Bowen recruited people with guarantors, taking property as security; the government advanced money beforehand, fixing term, head count, and weight in jin for delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen recruited contractors with guarantors and property as security, advanced government funds, and set deadlines, head counts, and delivery weights.

sentences.zh: 民多樂從，歲計充足。

translations.literal: The people mostly were glad to follow; yearly quotas were fully met.
translations.idiomatic: People readily participated, and annual quotas were met.

sentences.zh: 凡供禦膳及祀祭與泛用者，皆別其牢棧，以三千為額，所裁省冗費十之四。

translations.literal: For imperial banquets, sacrifices, and general use, separate pens and grades were made, with three thousand as the quota; redundant costs were cut by four-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial banquets, sacrifices, and general use were supplied from separate herds capped at three thousand head, cutting waste by forty percent.

sentences.zh: 其後，又用呂嘉問、劉永淵之言，治灶藏冰，以省工費。

translations.literal: Later, following the words of Lü Jiawen and Liu Yongyuan, ice storehouses were built to save labor costs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Lü Jiawen and Liu Yongyuan's advice, ice storehouses were built to reduce labor costs.

sentences.zh: 帝嚐患增置官司費財。

translations.literal: The emperor once worried that adding offices wasted wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once worried that creating new offices wasted money.

sentences.zh: 王安石謂增置官司，所以省費。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said that adding offices was how to save expense.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi argued that new offices would save money.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“古者什一而稅，今取財百端。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'In antiquity one-tenth was taxed; today wealth is taken by a hundred paths.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Antiquity took one-tenth in tax; today revenue is extracted by a hundred means.

sentences.zh: ”安石謂古非特什一而已。

translations.literal: Anshi said antiquity was not only one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied that antiquity took more than one-tenth.

sentences.zh: 帝又以倉吏給軍食，多侵盜，詔足其概量，嚴立諸倉丐取法。

translations.literal: The emperor also, because granary clerks supplying army food often embezzled, decreed that their measures be made full and strictly established begging laws for the various granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Because granary clerks often shortchanged army rations, the emperor ordered full measures and strict anti-embezzlement rules for all granaries.

sentences.zh: 中書因請增諸倉主典、役人祿至一萬八千九百緡，且盡增選人之祿，均其多寡。

translations.literal: The Secretariat therefore requested raising salaries of granary chiefs and laborers to 18,900 strings, and also broadly raising selectors' salaries to equalize their differences.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then proposed raising granary chiefs' and workers' salaries to 18,900 strings and broadly equalizing officials' pay.

sentences.zh: 令、錄增至十五千；

translations.literal: Magistrates and registrars were raised to fifteen thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and registrars were raised to fifteen thousand;

sentences.zh: 司理至簿、尉，防團軍監推、判官增至十二千。

translations.literal: judicial reviewers down to assistants and constables, and defense and militia supervisors' investigating and judging officials, were raised to twelve thousand.
translations.idiomatic: judicial reviewers through constables, and defense and militia investigating officials, to twelve thousand.

sentences.zh: 其後又增中書、審官東西、三班院、樞密院、三司、吏部流內銓、南曹、開封府吏祿，受財者以倉法論。

translations.literal: Later salaries of clerks in the Secretariat, Eastern and Western Personnel Evaluation Offices, Three Ranks Court, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, Ministry of Personnel's internal selection office, Southern Office, and Kaifeng Prefecture were also raised; those taking bribes were judged under granary law.
translations.idiomatic: Later clerks' salaries were raised across the central bureaucracy, with bribe-taking punished under granary law.

sentences.zh: 安石蓋欲盡祿天下之吏，帝以役法未就，緩其議。

translations.literal: Anshi broadly wished to pay salaries to all officials under Heaven; the emperor, because the labor-service law was not yet complete, slowed the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi wanted adequate salaries for all officials empire-wide; the emperor deferred the plan until the labor-service law was ready.

sentences.zh: 三司上新增吏祿數：京師歲增四十一萬三千四百餘緡，監司、諸州六十八萬九千八百餘緡。

translations.literal: The Three Departments reported figures for newly added clerks' salaries: the capital yearly increased 413,400-odd strings; circuit supervisors and prefectures 689,800-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments reported new clerks' salary costs: 413,400-plus strings yearly in the capital and 689,800-plus in circuits and prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時主新法者皆謂吏祿既厚，則人知自重，不敢冒法，可以省刑。

translations.literal: At that time proponents of the new laws all said that once clerks' salaries were thick, people would know to value themselves and not dare violate law, and punishment could thereby be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: New Law advocates argued that higher pay would make clerks respect their office, deter corruption, and reduce punishments.

sentences.zh: 然良吏實寡，賕取如故，往往陷重辟，議者不以為善。

translations.literal: Yet good officials were truly few; taking bribes remained as before; they often fell into heavy penalties—critics did not regard it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet honest officials remained few, bribery continued, and many faced severe penalties—critics judged the policy a failure.

sentences.zh: 初，陝西用兵，凡費緡錢七百餘萬。

translations.literal: At first, the Shaanxi campaign altogether cost more than seven million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi campaign initially cost over seven million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 帝以問王安石，安石曰：“楚建中考沈起簿書，計一道半歲費錢銀綢絹千二百萬貫、匹、兩。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wang Anshi; Anshi said: 'Chu Jianzhong examined Shen Qi's account books and calculated that one circuit for half a year spent 12,000,000 in cash, silver, silk, and bolts, taels.'
translations.idiomatic: Asked by the emperor, Wang Anshi cited Chu Jianzhong's audit of Shen Qi's books: one circuit spent twelve million in cash, silver, and silk in half a year.

sentences.zh: ”帝因欲知陝西歲用錢穀、金帛及增虧凡數，乃詔薛向條上。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore wished to know Shaanxi's yearly use of money, grain, gold, and silk and the figures of increase and loss; he decreed Xue Xiang to list them upward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wanted Shaanxi's annual spending in money, grain, gold, and silk tabulated and ordered Xue Xiang to report.

sentences.zh: 王安石以為擾，力請罷之，止詔三司帳司會計熙寧六年天下財用出入之數以聞。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi regarded it as disruptive and strongly requested its abolition; only an edict to the Three Departments' Accounts Office to compile Xining 6's revenue and expenditure under Heaven was left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi called the inquiry disruptive and had it canceled, leaving only an order for the Three Departments to report Xining 6 empire-wide accounts.

sentences.zh: 韓絳既相，建言：“三司總天下財賦，請選官置司，以天下戶口、人丁、稅賦、場務、坑冶、河渡、房園之類租額年課，及一路錢穀出入之數，去其重復，歲比較增虧、廢置及羨餘、橫費。

translations.literal: After Han Jiang became chief councilor, he proposed: 'The Three Departments control all wealth under Heaven; I request selecting officials to establish an office, taking household registers, adult males, tax levies, field offices, mines, river crossings, houses and gardens, and similar rent quotas and yearly levies, and each circuit's revenue and expenditure in money and grain, removing duplicates, yearly comparing increase, loss, abolition, establishment, surplus, and improper expense.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Jiang became chief councilor, he proposed a central accounting office to consolidate household, tax, monopoly, and circuit revenue data, compare yearly changes, and track waste.

sentences.zh: 計贏闕之處，使有無相通，而以任職能否為黜陟，則國計大綱可以省察。

translations.literal: Calculating where there is surplus or shortfall, making where there is none communicate with where there is, and taking ability in office as the basis for demotion and promotion—then the great outline of state accounts can be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Surpluses and deficits could be balanced across regions, and officials ranked on performance, giving the court a clear fiscal overview.

sentences.zh: ”三司使章惇亦以為言，乃詔置三司會計司，以絳提舉。

translations.literal: Three Departments Commissioner Zhang Dun also spoke likewise; thereupon an edict established the Three Departments Accounting Office, with Jiang as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments Commissioner Zhang Dun agreed, and the Three Departments Accounting Office was established under Jiang's supervision.

sentences.zh: 其後一州一路會計式成，上之，餘未就緒，未幾遂罷。

translations.literal: Later accounting forms for one prefecture and one circuit were completed and presented upward; the rest were not yet finished, and before long it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and circuit accounting forms were completed and submitted, but the system was abandoned before empire-wide accounts were finished.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制既行，三司所掌職務散於六曹、諸寺監。

translations.literal: Once the Yuanfeng official system was implemented, the duties managed by the Three Departments were dispersed among the six ministries and various directorates and offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanfeng bureaucratic reform, Three Departments functions were dispersed among the six ministries and various directorates.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，司馬光言：“今戶部尚書，舊三司使之任，左曹隸尚書，右曹不隸焉。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou, Sima Guang said: 'Today's Minister of Revenue holds the old Three Departments commissioner's duty; the left office is subordinate to the minister, the right office is not subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, Sima Guang said: "The Minister of Revenue holds the old Three Departments commissioner's role, but only the left office is subordinate—the right is not.

sentences.zh: 天下之財分而為二，視彼有餘，視此不足，不得移用。

translations.literal: Wealth under Heaven is divided in two; seeing that side has surplus, seeing this side has insufficiency, transfer cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: National wealth is split in two: one side has surplus, the other shortage, with no transfer between them.

sentences.zh: 宜令尚書兼領左右曹，侍郎分職而治，舊三司所掌錢穀財用事，有散於五曹及諸寺、監者，並歸戶部。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the minister concurrently to head both left and right offices, with vice ministers dividing duties and governing; money, grain, and wealth affairs once managed by the Three Departments but scattered among the five ministries and various directorates and offices should all return to the Ministry of Revenue.'
translations.idiomatic: The minister should head both offices with vice ministers dividing duties, and all scattered fiscal functions should return to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: ”遂詔尚書省立法。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Secretariat to establish law.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Secretariat to draft regulations.

sentences.zh: 有司請以府界、諸路在京庫務及常平等文帳悉歸戶部。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that capital-district, circuit, and capital storehouse accounts for the Ever-Normal Granary and similar institutions all be returned to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed returning capital, circuit, and Ever-Normal Granary accounts to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，熙寧五年，患天下文帳之繁，命曾布刪定法式。

translations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Xining, troubled by the complexity of account books under Heaven, the emperor ordered Zeng Bu to delete and fix standard forms.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5, troubled by complex account books empire-wide, the emperor ordered Zeng Bu to standardize forms.

sentences.zh: 布因請選吏於三司顓為一司，帳司之置始此。

translations.literal: Bu therefore requested selecting clerks in the Three Departments to specialize in one office; the establishment of the Accounts Office began here.
translations.idiomatic: Bu proposed a dedicated Accounts Office in the Three Departments—the origin of the centralized accounts bureau.

sentences.zh: 至元豐三年，首尾七八年，所設官吏僅六百人，費錢三十九萬緡，而勾磨出失陷錢止萬緡。

translations.literal: By the third year of Yuanfeng, over seven or eight years from start to finish, officials appointed numbered only six hundred, costing 390,000 strings, while audit uncovered only ten thousand strings in missing official money.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanfeng 3, after seven or eight years, six hundred officials had cost 390,000 strings while audits recovered only ten thousand in missing funds.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其無益，遂罷帳司，使州郡應上省帳皆歸轉運司，惟錢帛、糧草、酒曲、商稅等別為計帳上戶部。

translations.literal: The court knew it was useless and abolished the Accounts Office, making prefectures and circuits send accounts due at the capital to transport offices; only money, silk, grain, fodder, liquor yeast, and commercial tax were separately made into planning accounts sent to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing little benefit, the court abolished the Accounts Office, routed most provincial accounts through transport offices, and sent only key revenue categories directly to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 至是，令戶部盡收諸路文帳。

translations.literal: At this point, it was ordered that the Ministry of Revenue fully receive account books from the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was then ordered to receive all circuit account books.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍時為諫官，謂徒益紛紛，請如舊為便。

translations.literal: Su Zhe, then a remonstrator, said it would only increase confusion and requested that the old way be followed as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Su Zhe argued this would only add confusion and asked to keep the old system.

sentences.zh: 不行。

translations.literal: It was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His plea was rejected.

sentences.zh: 三年，戶部尚書韓忠彥、侍郎蘇轍、韓宗道言：“文武百官、宗室之蕃，一倍皇祐，四倍景德，班行、選人、胥吏率皆增益，而兩稅、征搉、山澤之利，與舊無以相過。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ministers of Revenue Han Zhongyan and Vice Ministers Su Zhe and Han Zongdao said: 'Civil and military officials and the imperial clan have doubled Huangyou and quadrupled Jingde; ranks of office, selectors, and clerks have mostly all increased, while the two taxes, exactions, and profits from mountains, marshes, and the like have not exceeded the old in any way.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Minister Han Zhongyan and Vice Ministers Su Zhe and Han Zongdao reported that officials and the imperial clan had doubled since Huangyou and quadrupled since Jingde, while land tax and monopoly revenues had not kept pace.

sentences.zh: 治平、熙寧之間，因時立政，凡改官者自三歲而為四歲，任子者自一歲一人而為三歲一人、自三歲一人而為六歲一人，宗室自袒免以上漸殺恩禮，此則今日之成法。

translations.literal: Between Zhiping and Xining, responding to the times, policies were established: those changing office went from three years to four; those receiving appointment by privilege went from one person per year to one per three years, and from one per three years to one per six; the imperial clan from those above bare-shoulder exemption gradually reduced favor and ritual—this is today's settled law.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhiping and Xining reforms had lengthened tenure, reduced hereditary appointments, and trimmed clan privileges—the laws now in force.

sentences.zh: 乞檢會寶元、慶曆、嘉祐故事，置司選官共議。

translations.literal: We request examining precedents of Baoyuan, Qingli, and Jiayou, establishing an office and selecting officials to discuss jointly.'
translations.idiomatic: They asked to review Baoyuan, Qingli, and Jiayou precedents and appoint a commission to discuss further cuts.

sentences.zh: ”詔戶部取應幹財用，除諸班諸軍料錢、衣賜、賞給、特支如舊外，餘費並裁省。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to take all relevant expenses; except for ration money, clothing grants, rewards, and special disbursements for the various ranks and armies as before, the rest were all to be cut and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was ordered to cut all expenses except army rations, clothing, rewards, and special disbursements.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“方將裁損八流，以清取士之路。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 'We are about to cut the eight currents to clear the path of selecting scholars.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict announced plans to streamline the eight paths of office and clarify examination routes.

sentences.zh: 命今後遇聖節、大禮、生辰，太皇太后、皇太后、皇太妃所得恩澤，並四分減一。

translations.literal: It was ordered that henceforth on sage festivals, great rites, and birthdays, the favors received by the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and Grand Imperial Consort were all reduced by one-fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth festival, ritual, and birthday favors to the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and Grand Imperial Consort were cut by one-fourth.

sentences.zh: ”於是上自宗室貴近，下至官曹胥吏，旁及宮室械器，皆命裁損。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from the imperial clan and noble kin above down to official clerks, and extending to palace furnishings and equipment, all were ordered cut and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Cuts were ordered from the imperial clan and nobility down through officials to palace furnishings and equipment.

sentences.zh: 久之，事未就。

translations.literal: After a long time, the matter was not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: After a long delay, little was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 議者謂裁減浮費所細碎苛急，甚損國體。

translations.literal: Critics said the cuts in floating expenses were minute, harsh, and urgent, greatly harming the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said the petty economies damaged state dignity.

sentences.zh: 於是已議未行者一切寢之。

translations.literal: Thereupon whatever had been discussed but not yet carried out was all put to rest.
translations.idiomatic: All pending cuts were then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後乃詔：“元祐裁損除授正任以下奉祿，失朝廷優禮，見條悉除之，循元豐舊制。

translations.literal: Later an edict said: 'The Yuanyou cuts to salaries below regular appointment in office lost the court's favor and courtesy; existing articles are all removed; follow the old Yuanfeng system.'
translations.idiomatic: A later edict restored Yuanfeng salary rules, revoking Yuanyou cuts below regular appointment rank as contrary to court courtesy.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 元豐鉤考隱漏官錢，督及一分者賞三厘。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng, auditing concealed and missing official money: those who recovered as much as one-tenth received a reward of three thousandths.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfeng, auditors who recovered concealed official funds received three-tenths of one percent of amounts found.

sentences.zh: 自元祐改法，賞薄而吏怠，遂復其舊。

translations.literal: From the Yuanyou reform of the law, rewards were thin and clerks grew slack, whereupon the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanyou weakened audit incentives, clerks grew lax and the old Yuanfeng reward scale was restored.

sentences.zh: 時議裁損吏祿，隸省、曹、寺、監者，止以元豐三年錢數為額，而吏三省者，凡兼領因事別給並舊請並罷。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to cut clerks' salaries: for those subordinate to ministries, bureaus, directorates, and commissions, only the cash amounts of Yuanfeng year three were taken as the quota, while for clerks of the Three Departments, all concurrent extra payments for particular affairs and old allowances were together abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Reformers sought to cap clerk pay at Yuanfeng third-year rates for ministry and agency staff, and to abolish all extra and legacy allowances for Three Departments clerks.

sentences.zh: 劉摯遂乞悉罷創增吏祿，詔韓維等究度，然不果罷。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi then petitioned to abolish entirely the newly added clerks' salaries; an edict ordered Han Wei and others to investigate and measure, yet in the end they were not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi asked to repeal all newly created clerk salaries; Han Wei and others were ordered to review the matter, but the cuts never took effect.

sentences.zh: 其後有司計中都吏祿，歲費緡錢三十二萬，詔以坊場稅錢給之。

translations.literal: Later the responsible offices calculated capital clerks' salaries, annual cost thirty-two myriad strings of cash, and an edict provided them from licensed-shop tax money.
