translations.idiomatic: Authorities later reckoned capital clerk salaries at 320,000 strings of cash per year, funded by licensed-shop taxes.

sentences.zh: 於是吏祿之冗濫者，率多革去矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the redundant and excessive among clerks' salaries were for the most part removed.
translations.idiomatic: Most redundant clerk pay was eliminated.

sentences.zh: 然三省吏猶有人受三奉而不改者，故孫升、傅堯俞皆以為言。

translations.literal: Yet among Three Departments clerks there were still some receiving three salaries without change, so Sun Sheng and Fu Yaoyu both spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: Some Three Departments clerks still drew triple salaries unchanged, prompting memorials from Sun Sheng and Fu Yaoyu.

sentences.zh: 至紹聖、元符，務反元祐之政，下至六曹吏，亦詔皆給見緡，如元豐之製。

translations.literal: By Shaosheng and Yuanfu they strove to reverse Yuanyou policies; down to Six Board clerks, edicts likewise provided current cash pay as under the Yuanfeng system.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaosheng and Yuanfu, Yuanyou policies were reversed; even Six Board clerks were ordered paid in cash at Yuanfeng rates.

sentences.zh: 先是，既罷導洛、堆垛等局，又罷熙河蘭會經製財用司，減放市易欠負及積欠租輸，選官體量茶鹽之法。

translations.literal: Previously, having already abolished the Guidao Canal, Stacking, and other bureaus, they also abolished the Xibo Lanhui Fiscal Control Commission, reduced and released market-trade debts and accumulated arrears in rent and tax deliveries, and selected officials to assess the tea and salt laws.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier reforms had abolished canal and warehouse bureaus and the Hexi fiscal commission, forgiven market-trade and tax arrears, and sent officials to review tea and salt policy.

sentences.zh: 使者之刻剝害民，如吳居厚、呂孝廉、王子京、李琮，內臣之生事斂怨，如李憲、宋用臣等，皆相繼正其罪。

translations.literal: Envoys who exploited and harmed the people, such as Wu Juhou, Lü Xiaolian, Wang Zijing, and Li Cong, and inner attendants who stirred up trouble and collected resentment, such as Li Xian, Song Yongchen, and others, were in succession punished for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Exploitative circuit envoys like Wu Juhou and meddlesome eunuchs like Li Xian were punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 既而稍復講修財利。

translations.literal: Before long they slightly restored attention to revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long fiscal exploitation resumed.

sentences.zh: 李清臣因白帝，今中外錢穀艱窘，戶部給百官奉，常無數月之備。

translations.literal: Li Qingchen thereupon informed the emperor: now internal and external money and grain are strained; the Ministry of Revenue in paying officials' salaries often has no reserve of several months.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen warned the emperor that treasury funds were so tight the Ministry of Revenue could barely cover a few months of official salaries.

sentences.zh: 章惇遂以財用匱乏，專指為司馬光、呂公著、呂大防、蘇轍諸人之罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun then took the depletion of finances and solely attributed it as the fault of Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Lü Dafang, Su Zhe, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun blamed the fiscal crisis entirely on Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Lü Dafang, Su Zhe, and other Yuanyou ministers.

sentences.zh: 左司諫翟思亦奏疏詆：“元祐以理財為諱，利入名額類多廢罷，督責之法不加於在職之臣，財利既多散失，且借貸百出，而熙、豐餘積，用之幾盡。

translations.literal: Left Shift Remonstrator Zhai Si also memorialized slandering: "In Yuanyou, treating fiscal management as taboo, revenue entries and quotas were mostly abolished; supervisory methods were not applied to officials in office; revenues were widely dispersed and lost, and borrowings issued in every direction, while the Xi and Feng surplus was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Si attacked Yuanyou fiscal policy for abolishing revenue offices, failing to hold officials accountable, squandering Xi-Feng surpluses, and borrowing recklessly.

sentences.zh: 方今內外財用，月計歲會，所入不足給所出。

translations.literal: At present internal and external finances, in monthly tallies and annual reckonings, income is insufficient to supply expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly and annual accounts now showed income failing to meet expenditure.

sentences.zh: 願下諸路會元祐以前所儲金穀及異時財利名額、歲入經數，著為成式。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would send down to all circuits to assemble the gold and grain stored before Yuanyou and the revenue quotas and annual income standard numbers of earlier times, and fix them as established formulas.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring pre-Yuanyou revenue quotas and stored surpluses as permanent standards.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，詔諸路轉運司以歲入財用置都籍，定諸州租額，且計一路凡數；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo, an edict ordered circuit transport commissions to establish master ledgers of annual revenue and expenditure, fix each prefecture's rent quotas, and tally each circuit's totals;
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong Jingguo 1, circuit transport offices were ordered to compile master ledgers of annual revenue, fix prefectural rent quotas, and report circuit-wide totals;

sentences.zh: 即有贏縮，書其籍。

translations.literal: when there were surpluses or deficits, record them in the ledger.
translations.idiomatic: recording any surplus or deficit in the ledger.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，又令：“歲以錢穀出入名數報提刑司保驗，以上戶部；

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, it was further ordered: "Each year report the names and numbers of money and grain receipts and disbursements to the judicial commission for verification and forwarding to the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 1, circuits were further ordered to report annual money and grain receipts and disbursements to judicial commissions for verification and forwarding to the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 戶部歲條諸路轉運使財賦虧贏，以行賞罰。

translations.literal: the Ministry of Revenue each year itemized transport commissioners' fiscal surpluses and deficits to carry out rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: and the ministry was to rank transport commissioners annually by fiscal surplus or deficit for rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 諸路無額錢物，立式下提刑司，括三年外未發數，期以一季聞奏。

translations.literal: Uncatalogued money and goods in the circuits—establish formulas sent to judicial commissions to tally amounts undisbursed beyond three years, with a deadline of one quarter to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Uncatalogued funds were to be inventoried by judicial commissions, with undisbursed balances over three years reported within one quarter.

sentences.zh: ”二年，官吏違負上供錢物，以分數為科罪之等，不及九分者罪以徒，多者更加之。

translations.literal: "In the second year, officials who defaulted on tribute money and goods were punished in grades by proportion; less than nine-tenths warranted penal servitude, with heavier penalties for larger shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, officials who fell short on tribute payments were punished by the proportion defaulted: less than nine-tenths complete incurred penal servitude, with heavier penalties for larger deficits.

sentences.zh: 歲首則列次年之數，聞於漕司，考實申部。

translations.literal: At the year's opening list the next year's figures, notify the transport commission, verify in fact and report to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At year's opening, next year's figures were to be listed, reported to transport commissions, verified, and forwarded to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 又以督限未嚴，更一季為一月。

translations.literal: Because supervision deadlines were not strict enough, one quarter was changed to one month.
translations.idiomatic: Because deadlines had proved too lax, the reporting period was shortened from one quarter to one month.

sentences.zh: 然國之經費，往往不給。

translations.literal: Yet state routine expenses often could not be met.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, routine state expenses often could not be covered.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔省罷官局，命戶部侍郎許幾專切提舉措置。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered reduction and abolition of government bureaus and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue Xu Ji specially to supervise and arrange measures.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, the court ordered bureau cuts and put Vice Minister Xu Ji in charge of fiscal retrenchment.

sentences.zh: 裁罷開封府重祿通引官客司並街道司額外兵士，及罷在京料次錢三十八處。

translations.literal: They cut the Kaifeng Prefecture Heavy-Salary Conduit and Guest Reception Office and the Street Office's extra soldiers, and abolished thirty-eight capital ration-payment sites.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng's heavy-salary conduit and guest offices and street patrol extras were cut, along with thirty-eight capital ration-payment sites.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，罷諸路州軍見貢六上局供奉物名件四百四十餘，存者才十一二，減數十二，停貢六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, they abolished more than four hundred forty tribute item names that prefectures and armies presented to the Six Upper Bureaus; only about one or two in ten remained; twelve quotas were reduced and six tribute items were halted.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 3, over 440 prefectural tribute items to the Six Upper Bureaus were abolished; only one or two in ten remained, twelve quotas were cut, and six tribute categories were ended.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎範坦言：“戶部歲入有限，支用無窮，一歲之入，僅了三季，餘仰朝廷應付。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Fan Kuan said: "The ministry's annual income is limited while expenditure is endless; one year's receipts barely cover three seasons, and the rest relies on the court to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Fan Kuan warned that ministry income covered only three quarters of the year, with the rest dependent on court transfers.

sentences.zh: 今歲支遣，較之去年又費百萬。

translations.literal: This year's disbursements, compared with last year, cost another million.
translations.idiomatic: This year's spending exceeded last year's by another million strings.

sentences.zh: ”有詔鐫減財賦，命御史中丞張克公與吳居厚、許幾等置局議論。

translations.literal: "An edict ordered carved reduction of fiscal revenue and expenditure and appointed Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong, together with Wu Juhou, Xu Ji, and others, to establish a bureau for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered fiscal cuts and a review bureau headed by Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong, Wu Juhou, and Xu Ji.

sentences.zh: 克公抗言：“官冗者汰，奉厚者減，今官較之元祐已多十倍，國用安得不乏。

translations.literal: Kegong spoke forthrightly: "Where offices are redundant, weed them out; where salaries are thick, reduce them—today offices compared with Yuanyou are already more than tenfold; how can state use not be depleted?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kegong insisted that redundant offices be cut and lavish salaries reduced, noting that posts had grown tenfold since Yuanyou and the treasury could not but be strained.

sentences.zh: 乞將節度使下至遙郡刺史，除軍功轉授者，各減奉半，然後閑慢局務、工伎末作，亦宜減省。

translations.literal: I beg that from military commissioners down to distant-prefecture prefects, except those transferred for military merit, each have salaries reduced by half; then idle and slow bureaus, craftsmen, and petty trades should also be reduced and economized.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to halve salaries from military commissioners down to distant prefects except merit appointees, then to cut idle bureaus and artisan offices.

sentences.zh: 自貴及賤，自近及遠，行之公當，人自無詞。

translations.literal: From noble to humble, from near to far—if carried out fairly and appropriately, people will themselves have nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Applied fairly from the highest to the lowest, near and far, no one could fairly object.

sentences.zh: ”時論韙之。

translations.literal: "Contemporary opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries applauded his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時諸路轉運司類以乏告，詔戶部編次一歲財用出納之數，諸路州縣各為都籍，以待考較；

translations.literal: At the time circuit transport commissions mostly reported shortages; an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to compile annual fiscal receipts and disbursements; each circuit's prefectures and counties were to keep master ledgers for examination and comparison;
translations.idiomatic: As transport commissions widely reported shortfalls, the ministry was ordered to compile annual fiscal accounts and require prefectures and counties to keep master ledgers for audit;

sentences.zh: 工部金、銀、銅、鉛、水銀、朱砂等，亦嚴帳籍之法；

translations.literal: the Ministry of Works' gold, silver, copper, lead, mercury, cinnabar, and the like also had strict ledger methods;
translations.idiomatic: the Ministry of Works likewise tightened ledger rules for gold, silver, copper, lead, mercury, cinnabar, and similar commodities;

sentences.zh: 令諸路各條三十年以還一歲出入及泛用之數。

translations.literal: and ordered each circuit to itemize annual receipts, disbursements, and general-use amounts for the past thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: and each circuit was to report thirty years of annual receipts, disbursements, and miscellaneous spending.

sentences.zh: 初，比部掌勾稽天下文帳，吏習偷惰，自崇寧至政和，稽違積數凡二千六百七十有餘。

translations.literal: Initially the Audit Bureau managed auditing all accounts under Heaven; clerks were accustomed to theft and sloth, and from Chongning to Zhenghe accumulated overdue audit items totaled more than two thousand six hundred seventy.
translations.idiomatic: The Audit Bureau's clerks had grown habitually lax; from Chongning to Zhenghe more than 2,670 accounts remained unaudited.

sentences.zh: 於是申敕六曹，以拘督一歲多寡為寺、監賞罰。

translations.literal: Thereupon they issued instructions to the Six Boards that, taking supervision of one year's quantity as the measure, directorates and commissions would receive rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Boards were then ordered to reward or punish directorates and commissions according to how much of the year's backlog they cleared.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，命戶部參稽熙、豐及今財用有餘不足之數，又立旁通格，令諸路漕司各條元豐、紹聖、崇寧、政和一歲財用出入多寡來上。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to examine and compare Xi and Feng and present finances for surplus and shortfall, and a lateral-connecting standard was also established, ordering each circuit transport commission to itemize Yuanfeng, Shaosheng, Chongning, and Zhenghe annual fiscal receipts and disbursements, more or less, and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 7, the ministry was ordered to compare Xi-Feng and current finances and to require transport commissions to report annual receipts and disbursements for Yuanfeng, Shaosheng, Chongning, and Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 淮南漕臣張根言：“天下之費，莫大於土木之功。

translations.literal: Huainan transport commissioner Zhang Gen said: "Under Heaven, no expense is greater than earth-and-wood construction.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan transport commissioner Zhang Gen declared that no state expense exceeded construction projects.

sentences.zh: 其次如人臣賜第，一第無慮數十萬緡，稍增雄麗，非百萬不可。

translations.literal: Next, such as mansions granted to ministers—one mansion is not less than several hundred thousand strings; slightly increasing grandeur and beauty cannot be done for less than a million.
translations.idiomatic: Next came ministerial mansions, each costing hundreds of thousands of strings and easily a million if made more splendid.

sentences.zh: 佐命如趙普，定策如韓琦，不聞峻宇雕牆，僭擬宮省，奈何剝民膚髓，為廝役之奉乎？

translations.literal: Assistants in founding the dynasty such as Zhao Pu, and framers of policy such as Han Qi—one does not hear of lofty halls and carved walls, presumptuously imitating palace offices; why flay the people's flesh and marrow to supply menial servants?
translations.idiomatic: Founding ministers like Zhao Pu and Han Qi built no palatial mansions rivaling the palace—why strip the people to house servants?

sentences.zh: 其次如田產、房廊，雖不若賜第之多，然日削月朘，所在無幾。

translations.literal: Next, such as fields and shops—though not like granted mansions in amount, yet day by day shaved and month by month pared, in each place little remains.
translations.idiomatic: Landholdings and rental properties, though less costly than mansions, were being steadily depleted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 又如金帛以供一時之好賜，有不可已者，而亦不可不節。

translations.literal: Again, gold and silk to supply momentary favor and gifts—some cannot be stopped, yet also cannot go unregulated.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silk for spontaneous gifts could not be abolished entirely, yet had to be restrained.

sentences.zh: 至如賜帶，其直雖不過數百緡，然天下金寶糜費日久，夫豈易得？

translations.literal: As for bestowed belts, their value may be no more than several hundred strings, yet the empire's gold and jewels have been wasted and depleted over long days—how could they be easily obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Even bestowed belts worth only a few hundred strings drew on gold and jewels the empire had long been exhausting.

sentences.zh: 今乃賚及仆隸，使混淆公卿間，貴賤、賢不肖，莫之辨也。

translations.literal: Now rewards reach even servants and runners, causing confusion among ministers and grandees; noble and base, worthy and unworthy, none can be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards now reached even servants, blurring rank among ministers so that noble and base, worthy and unworthy, could no longer be told apart.

sentences.zh: 如以為左右趨走之人，不欲其墨綬，當別為制度，以示等威。

translations.literal: If one thinks of those who hurry left and right in attendance and does not wish them to wear black ribbons, separate regulations should be made to display ranks and majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If attendants were not to wear official ribbons, separate insignia should mark their rank.

sentences.zh: ”疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: "The memorial was submitted; [the emperor] took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，思節冗費，中都吏重復增給及泛濫員額，並詔裁損。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, he thought to economize redundant expenses; capital clerks' repeated additional payments and swollen quotas were all ordered cut.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign the emperor ordered cuts to redundant spending, duplicate capital clerk allowances, and bloated quotas.

sentences.zh: 後苑嚐計增葺殿宇，計用金箔五十六萬七千。

translations.literal: The Rear Park once calculated additions and repairs to palace halls, estimating use of gold leaf at five hundred sixty-seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Rear Park once estimated repairs to palace halls would require 567,000 units of gold leaf.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“用金為箔，以飾土木，一壞不可復收，甚亡謂也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Using gold as leaf to adorn earth and wood—once ruined it cannot be recovered; this is very pointless.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that gilding timber with gold leaf wastes metal that cannot be recovered once the building decays—this was absurd.

sentences.zh: ”令內侍省罰請者。

translations.literal: "He ordered the Palace Domestic Service to punish those who had requested it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Palace Domestic Service to punish those who had submitted the request.

sentences.zh: 及蔡京為相，增修財利之政，務以侈靡惑人主，動以《周官》惟王不會為說，每及前朝惜財省費者，必以為陋。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing became chancellor, he increased and revised revenue policies, striving to beguile the ruler with extravagance, constantly citing the 《Offices of Zhou》 doctrine that the king alone does not keep accounts, and whenever former courts' thrift and economy were mentioned, he always deemed them shabby.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cai Jing became chancellor, he expanded revenue extraction and court luxury, citing the 《Offices of Zhou》 that the king alone keeps no accounts, and dismissing earlier thrift as mean-spirited.

sentences.zh: 至於土木營造，率欲度前規而侈後觀。

translations.literal: As for earth-and-wood construction, they generally wished to surpass former standards and make later views extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Building projects were routinely designed to exceed earlier standards and impress later observers.

sentences.zh: 元豐改官制，在京官司供給之數，皆並為職錢，視嘉祐、治平時賦祿優矣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng revision of the bureaucracy, capital offices' supply amounts were all merged into position money, which compared with Jiayou and Zhiping era salary allotments was already more generous.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng bureaucracy had already merged capital office supplies into position salaries more generous than Jiayou and Zhiping allotments.

sentences.zh: 京更增供給、食料等錢，於是宰執皆然。

translations.literal: Jing further increased supply, food, and other payments, whereupon all chief councillors were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing added further supply and food allowances, and the chief councillors followed suit.

sentences.zh: 京既罷相，帝惡其變亂法度，將盡更革。

translations.literal: Once Jing had left the chancellorship, the emperor hated his overturning of laws and institutions and was about to change them all.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai Jing left office, the emperor, resenting his disruption of institutions, prepared sweeping reversals.

sentences.zh: 命戶部侍郎許幾裁損浮費及百官濫祿，悉循元豐之舊，宰執亦聽辭所增奉。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Xu Ji to cut floating expenses and officials' excessive salaries, all following Yuanfeng's old rules; chief councillors were also permitted to decline their increased salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Ji was ordered to cut wasteful spending and excessive salaries and restore Yuanfeng norms; chief councillors could renounce their added pay.

sentences.zh: 京不便，與其黨倡言：“減奉非治世事。

translations.literal: Jing was displeased and, with his faction, proclaimed: "Reducing salaries is not the business of ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing objected, and his faction argued that cutting salaries was no way to govern.

sentences.zh: 司馬光請聽宰臣辭南郊給賜，神宗卒不允，且增選人及庶人在官者之奉。

translations.literal: Sima Guang asked to allow chief ministers to decline Southern Suburb grant gifts; Shenzong in the end did not approve, and moreover increased the salaries of examination candidates and commoners holding office.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Shenzong's refusal when Sima Guang asked ministers to decline Southern Suburb gifts, and his increase of pay for examination candidates and commoners in office.

sentences.zh: 帝以繼述為事，當奉承神宗。

translations.literal: The emperor, taking succession as his task, should uphold Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, committed to continuing Shenzong's legacy, should follow his example.

sentences.zh: ”由是官吏奉給並仍舊，而宰執亦增如故。

translations.literal: "Thereupon officials' and clerks' salaries all remained as before, and chief councillors' increases likewise continued as formerly.
translations.idiomatic: Official and clerk salaries therefore remained unchanged, and chief councillors kept their added pay.

sentences.zh: 初，宰執堂食亦皆有常數。

translations.literal: Initially, chief councillors' hall meals also all had fixed amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillors' hall meals had once been fixed allowances.

sentences.zh: 至是，品目猥多，有公使、乏支之別，台、省、寺、監又增廚錢。

translations.literal: By this time categories were numerous and miscellaneous, with distinctions of public envoys and shortage payments; the Censorate, ministries, directorates, and commissions further increased kitchen money.
translations.idiomatic: By then items had multiplied, with separate envoy and shortfall allowances, and censorate, ministry, and agency kitchen funds had grown.

sentences.zh: 侍御史毛注嚐奏論之，不行。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Mao Zhu once memorialized discussing it; it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Mao Zhu once protested, without effect.

sentences.zh: 蔡京復得政，言者遂以裁損祿廩為幾罪，幾坐奪職。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing regained power, critics then made cutting salaries and grain stores Ji's offense, and Ji was demoted from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to power, critics made Xu Ji's salary cuts a crime, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 於時天下久平，吏員冗溢，節度使至八十餘員，留後、觀察下及遙郡刺史多至數千員，學士、待制中外百五十員。

translations.literal: At that time the empire had long been at peace; official posts were redundant and overflowing—military commissioners reached more than eighty, deputies, observation commissioners, and below down to distant-prefecture prefects often reached several thousand, and academicians and awaiting-draft compilers inside and outside totaled one hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace, posts had swollen to more than eighty military commissioners, thousands of deputies and distant prefects, and 150 academicians and awaiting-draft compilers.

sentences.zh: 京又專用豐亨豫大之說，諛悅帝意，始廣茶利，歲以一百萬緡進禦，以京城所主之。

translations.literal: Jing again exclusively used the doctrine of abundance, prosperity, and grandeur, flattering the emperor's intent; he first expanded tea profits, each year presenting one million strings to the throne, administered by the Capital Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing preached abundance and grandeur to please the emperor, expanded tea revenues, and presented a million strings yearly to the throne through the Capital Bureau.

sentences.zh: 其後又有應奉司、御前生活所、營繕所、蘇杭造作局、御前人船所，其名雜出，大率爭以奇侈為功。

translations.literal: Later there were also the Tribute Service, the Imperial Front Provision Office, the Construction Office, the Suzhou-Hangzhou Manufacture Bureau, and the Imperial Front Personnel and Shipping Office—names issued in confusion, for the most part competing to make odd extravagance their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Later came the Tribute Service, Imperial Provision Office, Construction Office, Suzhou-Hangzhou Manufacture Bureau, and Imperial Shipping Office—agencies that vied in exotic extravagance.

sentences.zh: 歲運花石綱，一石之費，民間至用三十萬緡。

translations.literal: Each year they transported the Flower and Stone Fleet; the cost of one stone among the people could reach three hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The annual Flower and Stone Fleet could cost the people as much as 300,000 strings to move a single stone.

sentences.zh: 奸吏旁緣，牟取無藝，民不勝弊。

translations.literal: Wicked clerks attached themselves on the side and seized profit without limit; the people could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks exploited the system without limit until the people were crushed.

sentences.zh: 用度日繁，左藏庫異時月費緡錢三十六萬，至是，衍為一百二十萬。

translations.literal: Daily expenditure grew ever more numerous; the Left Treasury at one time spent three hundred sixty thousand strings per month—in this period it extended to one million two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Spending soared that the Left Treasury's monthly outlay rose from 360,000 strings to 1.2 million.

sentences.zh: 又三省、密院吏員猥雜，有官至中大夫，一身而兼十餘奉，故當時議者有“俸入超越從班，品秩幾於執政”之言。

translations.literal: Again, Three Departments and Privy Council clerks were numerous and mixed; some reached Senior Grand Master of the Palace, one person holding more than ten salaries together—so critics of the time had the saying, "Salary income surpasses the entourage ranks; rank and grade nearly equal the chief councillors."
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments and Privy Council clerks had multiplied; some Senior Grand Masters drew more than ten salaries, prompting critics to say clerk pay outranked entourage officials and nearly matched the chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 又增置兼局，禮製、明堂，詳定《國朝會要》、《九域圖志》、《一司敕令》之類，職秩繁委，廩給無度。

translations.literal: They also added concurrent bureaus—rites regulations, the Bright Hall, detailed compilation of the 《National Compilation of Important Matters》, the 《Atlas of the Nine Regions》, the 《Single-Bureau Statutes》, and the like—posts numerous and entangled, grain payments without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent bureaus were added to compile rites, the Bright Hall, the 《National Compilation of Important Matters》, the 《Atlas of the Nine Regions》, the 《Single-Bureau Statutes》, and similar works, multiplying posts and salaries without limit.

sentences.zh: 侍御史黃葆光論其弊，帝善之而未行；

translations.literal: Attending Censor Huang Baoguang discussed their abuses; the emperor approved but did not carry it out;
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Huang Baoguang criticized these abuses; the emperor approved but took no action;

sentences.zh: 俄而詔云：當豐亨豫大之時，為衰亂減損之計”，自是罕敢言者。

translations.literal: soon an edict said: "In a time of abundance, prosperity, and grandeur, to plan cuts as for decline and disorder"—from then few dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: soon an edict declared that in an age of abundance one must not plan as for decline—and few dared speak of cuts thereafter.

sentences.zh: 然吏祿泛冒已極，以史院言之，供檢吏三省幾千人。

translations.literal: Yet clerks' salaries had become extravagantly excessive to the extreme; taking the History Institute as an example, supply and examination clerks from the Three Departments numbered nearly several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk salaries had nonetheless reached their peak; the History Institute alone employed nearly a thousand Three Departments clerks for document retrieval.

sentences.zh: 蔡京又動以筆帖於榷貨務支賞給，有一紙至萬緡者。

translations.literal: Cai Jing also frequently used written slips at the Monopoly Trade Office to draw rewards and payments; one slip could reach ten thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing routinely drew payments from the Monopoly Trade Office on written orders, some for as much as 10,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 京所侵私，以千萬計，朝論喧然。

translations.literal: Jing's private encroachments were reckoned in tens of millions; court opinion was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: His private takings were reckoned in the tens of millions, and court opinion boiled over.

sentences.zh: 乃詔三省、樞密院吏額用元豐法，其歲賜悉裁之，時翕然以為快。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Three Departments and Privy Council clerk quotas to use the Yuanfeng law, and all their annual grants were cut—at the time all together regarded it as a relief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then restored Yuanfeng clerk quotas for the Three Departments and Privy Council and cut annual grants, to widespread approval.

sentences.zh: 臣僚上言：“諸州遇天寧節，除公使外，別給係省錢，充錫宴之用。

translations.literal: A minister memorialized: "When prefectures observe the Tianning Festival, besides public envoys' funds, separate payments of tied-province money are given to supply banquet grants.
translations.idiomatic: A minister reported that on the Tianning Festival prefectures besides envoy funds also drew tied-province money for banquets.

sentences.zh: 獨諸路監司許支逐司錢物，一筵之饌，有及數百千者，浮侈相誇，無有藝極。

translations.literal: Only circuit supervisory commissioners were permitted to disburse their own offices' money and goods; one banquet's fare could reach several hundred or thousand, extravagance competing in display, without limit or end.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioners alone could spend office funds on feasts costing hundreds or thousands of strings, vying in wasteful display without limit.

sentences.zh: ”自是詔：“遇天寧節宴，舊應給錢者，發運、監司每司不得過三百貫，餘每司不得過二百貫，以上舊給數少者，止依舊。

translations.literal: "Thereupon an edict said: "For Tianning Festival banquets, where money was formerly supplied, transport and supervisory offices per office may not exceed three hundred guan, the rest per office may not exceed two hundred guan; where the former allotment was less, follow only the old amount.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then capped Tianning banquet funds at 300 guan per transport or supervisory office and 200 guan for others, retaining lower prior limits where applicable.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 自崇寧以來，言利之臣殆析秋毫，沿汴州縣創增鎮柵以牟稅利。

translations.literal: From Chongning onward, revenue-minded ministers nearly split autumn hairs; along the Bian River prefectures and counties they newly added market barriers to seek tax profit.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chongning, revenue officials had taxed every petty item, and Bian River counties added market barriers to extract tolls.

sentences.zh: 官賣石炭增二十餘場，而天下市易務，炭皆官自賣。

translations.literal: Government sale of coal increased by more than twenty depots, and throughout the empire at market-trade offices, coal was all sold by the government itself.
translations.idiomatic: Government coal depots increased by more than twenty, and market-trade offices nationwide sold coal only through the state.

sentences.zh: 名品瑣碎，則有四腳鋪床、榨磨、水磨、廟圖、淘沙金等錢，不得而盡記也。

translations.literal: Item names were minute and trivial—there were taxes on four-legged shop beds, oil presses and mills, water mills, temple maps, panning sand for gold, and the like; they cannot all be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Petty levies multiplied—on shop stalls, presses, water mills, temple maps, gold-panning, and more than can be listed.

sentences.zh: 宣和以後，王黼專主應奉，掊剝橫賦，以羨為功。

translations.literal: After Xuanhe, Wang Fu exclusively directed the Tribute Service, stripping and prying with arbitrary levies, taking surplus as achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanhe, Wang Fu ran the Tribute Service, extorting arbitrary levies and treating surplus revenue as merit.

sentences.zh: 嶺南、川蜀農民陂罰錢，罷學製學事司贍學錢，皆歸應奉司。

translations.literal: Lingnan and Sichuan farmers' dyke penalty money, abolished-study and regulated-study affair office school-support money—all went to the Tribute Service.
translations.idiomatic: Dyke penalties in Lingnan and Sichuan and abolished-school support funds were all diverted to the Tribute Service.

sentences.zh: 所入雖多，國用日匱。

translations.literal: Although receipts were many, state use daily grew depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Though receipts increased, the treasury grew daily poorer.

sentences.zh: 六年，尚書左丞宇文粹中言：

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Director of the Left Department Yuwen Cuizhong said:
translations.idiomatic: In year six, Vice Director Yuwen Cuizhong memorialized:

sentences.zh: “近歲南伐蠻獠，北贍幽燕，關陝、綿、茂邊事日起，山東、河北寇盜竊發。

translations.literal: "In recent years the south attacked Man and Liao peoples, the north supplied You and Yan, border affairs in Guanxi, Mian, and Mao rose day by day, and bandits and robbers stole forth in Shandong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: "In recent years campaigns against southern tribes, subsidies for the northern frontier, rising troubles on the Guanxi and Mian-Mao borders, and banditry in Shandong and Hebei

sentences.zh: 賦斂歲入有限，支梧繁夥，一切取足於民。

translations.literal: Tax levies' annual income was limited while supports were numerous and many; everything was taken in full from the people.
translations.idiomatic: had strained limited tax revenues, and every need was squeezed from the people.

sentences.zh: 陝西上戶多棄產而居京師，河東富人多棄產而入川蜀。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's upper households mostly abandoned property and dwelt in the capital; Hedong's rich mostly abandoned property and entered Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy Shaanxi households abandoned their lands for the capital; Hedong magnates fled into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 河北衣被天下，而蠶織皆廢；

translations.literal: Hebei clothed all under Heaven, yet sericulture and weaving were all abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had clothed the empire, yet sericulture and weaving collapsed;

sentences.zh: 山東頻遭大水，而耕種失時；

translations.literal: Shandong frequently suffered great floods, yet plowing and sowing missed their seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Shandong suffered repeated floods and missed planting seasons;

sentences.zh: 他路取辦目前，不務存恤。

translations.literal: other circuits took provision for the present moment and did not attend to preservation and relief.
translations.idiomatic: and other circuits extorted for immediate needs without regard for relief.

sentences.zh: 穀麥未登，已先俵糴；

translations.literal: Grain and wheat had not yet ripened, yet grain was already advanced and purchased in advance;
translations.idiomatic: Grain was requisitioned and bought on credit before the harvest ripened;

sentences.zh: 歲賦已納，復理欠負。

translations.literal: The year's levy already paid, again they pursued arrears.
translations.idiomatic: After the annual tax was paid, officials still collected old arrears.

sentences.zh: 托應奉而買珍異奇寶，欠民積者一路至數十萬計；

translations.literal: Entrusting the Tribute Service to buy rare and wondrous treasures, debts owed the people in one circuit reached tallies in the hundreds of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute Service was used to procure exotic treasures, leaving debts to commoners in a single circuit running into the hundreds of thousands;

sentences.zh: 假上供而織文繡錦綺，役工女者一郡至百餘人。

translations.literal: Feigning court tribute to weave patterned embroidery, brocade, and gauze, conscripted artisan women in one prefecture reached more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Court tribute was cited to command brocades and figured silks, with more than a hundred skilled women conscripted in a single prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛下勤恤民隱，詔令數下，悉為虛文。

translations.literal: Your Majesty diligently comforted the people's hidden woes; edicts issued repeatedly—all became empty documents.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty repeatedly issued edicts to ease the people's suffering, they amounted to empty words.

sentences.zh: 民不聊生，不惟寇盜繁滋，竊恐災異數起。

translations.literal: The people could not sustain life; not only did bandits and robbers multiply—I privately fear portents and anomalies will arise in number.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot survive; banditry thrives, and I fear Heaven's warnings will multiply.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之時，國計所仰，皆有實數。

translations.literal: In the times of the forefathers, what the state accounts relied upon all had real numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperors, state revenue rested on fixed, verified figures.

sentences.zh: 有額上供四百萬，無額上供二百萬，京師商稅、店宅務、抵當所諸處雜收錢一百餘萬。

translations.literal: Quota court tribute four million, non-quota court tribute two million; capital commercial tax, the Shop and Residence Office, pawn offices, and miscellaneous receipts everywhere—over one million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed tribute quotas brought four million strings, extra tribute two million, and miscellaneous revenues from capital commerce, pawnshops, and related offices exceeded one million more.

sentences.zh: 三司以七百萬之入，供一年之費，而儲其餘以待不測之用。

translations.literal: The Commission for Fiscal Affairs used seven million in receipts to supply one year's expenditures, storing the remainder to await unforeseen use.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiscal Commission covered annual expenses from seven million strings in revenue and stored the surplus for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 又有解池鹽鈔、晉礬、市舶遺利，內贍京師，外實邊鄙，間遇水旱，隨以振濟，蓋量入為出，沛然有餘。

translations.literal: Moreover there were Jie Pond salt tickets, Jin alum, and maritime-trade windfalls—inward sustaining the capital, outward filling the border marches; occasionally meeting flood or drought, relief followed at once. Generally measuring income to set outlays, abundantly with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Salt certificates, Shanxi alum, and maritime-trade profits sustained the capital and frontier alike; flood and drought relief could be met from surplus, for revenue once matched spending with room to spare.

sentences.zh: 近年諸局務、應奉等司截撥上供，而繁富路分一歲所入，亦不敷額。

translations.literal: In recent years various bureaus and the Tribute Service and the like diverted court tribute, yet even wealthy circuits' one-year receipts still did not meet quota.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years tribute bureaus diverted court funds, and even the wealthiest circuits failed to meet their quotas.

sentences.zh: 然創置書局者比職事官之數為多，檢計修造者比實用之物增倍，其他妄耗百出，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yet established printing bureaus compared to functional officials were more numerous; audited repairs and constructions compared to useful items doubled; other reckless expenditures issued by the hundred, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Printing offices outnumbered functional officials, audited construction doubled what was actually needed, and countless other wastes proliferated beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 若非痛行裁減，慮智者無以善其後。

translations.literal: If one does not sternly carry out cuts and reductions, I fear the wise will have no way to mend what follows.
translations.idiomatic: Without drastic cuts, even the wise will be unable to repair the aftermath.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 久之，乃詔蔡攸等就尚書省置講議財利司，除茶法已有定制，餘並講究條上。

translations.literal: After long delay, an edict ordered Cai You and others to establish at the Department of State Affairs a Bureau for Discussing Fiscal Profit; apart from the tea law, which already had fixed regulations, all else was to be investigated and memorialized item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the throne ordered Cai You and others to set up a Fiscal Review Bureau at the Department of State Affairs; except for the established tea regulations, all other levies were to be examined and reported.

sentences.zh: 攸請：內侍職掌，事幹宮禁，應裁省者，委童貫取旨。

translations.literal: You requested: eunuch offices, matters touching the palace precincts—what should be cut was entrusted to Tong Guan to take instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You proposed that cuts to eunuch offices and palace affairs be referred to Tong Guan for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 時貫以廣陽郡王領右府故也。

translations.literal: At the time Guan, as Prince of Guangyang, led the Right Bureau—hence this.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Tong Guan, as Prince of Guangyang, headed the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 於是不急之務，無名之費，悉議裁省。

translations.literal: Thereupon non-urgent tasks and nameless expenses were all discussed for cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Nonessential projects and pointless spending were then reviewed for elimination.

sentences.zh: 帝亦自罷諸路應奉官吏，省六尚歲貢。

translations.literal: The emperor himself also abolished Tribute Service officers on all circuits and reduced the Six Workshops' annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also abolished Tribute Service agents in every circuit and cut the Six Workshops' annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔諸路帥臣、監司各條所部當裁省凡目以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict ordered circuit commanders and supervisory commissioners each to list items in their jurisdictions to be cut and report.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, circuit commanders and supervisory commissioners were ordered to itemize proposed cuts in their jurisdictions and report.

sentences.zh: 後苑書藝局等月省十九萬緡，歲可省二百二十萬。

translations.literal: The Rear Park Calligraphy and Arts Bureau and the like saved one hundred ninety thousand strings monthly—two million two hundred thousand yearly.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial ateliers alone saved 190,000 strings per month, or 2.2 million per year.

sentences.zh: 應奉司所管諸色窠名錢數內：兩浙路錢旁定帖息錢，湖、常、溫、秀州無額上供錢，淮南路添酒錢等，並行截節，更不充應奉支用。

translations.literal: Within the various nominal-account monies managed by the Tribute Service: Liangzhe circuit's side-fixed deposit interest money; Wu, Chang, Wen, and Xiu prefectures' non-quota court tribute money; Huainan circuit's added wine tax and the like—all were cut off at once and no longer supplied Tribute Service expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Among Tribute Service accounts, Liangzhe deposit interest, non-quota tribute from Lake, Chang, Wen, and Xiu prefectures, Huainan's supplemental wine tax, and similar levies were all terminated and no longer funded the Tribute Service.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔曰：“比年寬大之詔數下，裁省之令屢行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict said: "In recent years magnanimous edicts have been issued repeatedly, and austerity orders enacted again and again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict declared: "Magnanimous edicts have been issued repeatedly in recent years, and austerity orders enforced again and again.

sentences.zh: 有司便文而實惠不至，蓋緣任用非人，興作事端，蠹耗邦財。

translations.literal: The offices made expedient phrasing while real benefit did not arrive—because appointees were unfit, they stirred up affairs and devoured state wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Offices complied on paper while the people saw no relief, for unworthy appointees stirred up trouble and devoured state wealth.

sentences.zh: 假享上之名，濟營私之欲，漁奪百姓，無所不至。

translations.literal: Borrowing the name of serving the court, they aided private desires; plundering the hundred surnames, they reached everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: They abused the name of imperial service to pursue private gain and plundered the people without limit.

sentences.zh: 朕夙夜痛悼，思有以撫循慰安之。

translations.literal: I, from early dawn to late night, grieve in pain and think how to soothe, comfort, and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve day and night and seek ways to comfort and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 應茶鹽立額結絕。

translations.literal: Tea and salt fixed quotas are concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed tea and salt quotas are abolished.

sentences.zh: 應奉司兩浙諸路置局及花石綱等，諸路非泛上供拋降物色，延福宮西城所租課，內外修造諸處采斫木植、製造局所，並罷。

translations.literal: Tribute Service bureaus in Liangzhe circuits, the Flower and Stone Convoys, non-routine court tribute and surrendered goods on all circuits, rent from Yanfu Palace and the Western Park Office, timber harvesting and manufacturing bureaus inside and outside—all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute Service offices in Liangzhe, the Flower and Stone Convoys, irregular tribute and surrendered goods, rents from Yanfu Palace and the Western Park, and timber and manufacturing bureaus everywhere were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 諸局及西城所見管錢物並付有司，其拘收到百姓地上，並給還舊佃人。

translations.literal: Monies and goods now managed by the various bureaus and the Western Park Office are all handed to the regular offices; land seized from commoners is all returned to the original tenants.
translations.idiomatic: Funds held by abolished bureaus were transferred to regular agencies, and land seized from commoners was returned to former tenants.

sentences.zh: 減掖庭用度，減侍從官以上月廩，及罷諸兼局，以上並令有司據所得數撥充諸路糴本，及樁充募兵賞軍之用。

translations.literal: Reduce Inner Palace expenditures, reduce monthly stipends for attendant officials and above, abolish concurrent posts, and apply the above savings, according to amounts received, to grain-purchase capital in the circuits and to earmark recruitment and military rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Palace spending, officials' stipends, and concurrent posts were cut, with savings allocated to grain purchases in the circuits and to recruitment and military rewards.

sentences.zh: 應齋醮道場，除舊法合有外，並罷道官及撥賜宮觀等房錢、田土之類。

translations.literal: Vegetarian feasts and Daoist rites: apart from what old law provides, abolish Daoist officials and grants of palace and temple housing, fields, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual feasts and Daoist ceremonies beyond what law allows were ended, along with stipends to Daoist officials and grants of temple property.

sentences.zh: 六尚，並依祖宗法。

translations.literal: The Six Workshops—all follow the forefathers' law.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Workshops were restored to ancestral regulations.

sentences.zh: 罷大晟府，罷教學所，罷教坊額外人。

translations.literal: Abolish the Great Splendor Office, abolish the Teaching Institute, abolish extra personnel in the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Splendor Office, the Teaching Institute, and excess Music Bureau staff were abolished.

sentences.zh: 罷行幸局，罷采石所，罷待詔額外人。

translations.literal: Abolish the Imperial Progress Bureau, abolish the Quarry Office, abolish extra awaiting-edict personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Progress Bureau, the Quarry Office, and excess awaiting-edict posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 罷都茶場，依舊歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Abolish the Capital Tea Market; it returns as before to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Tea Market was abolished and restored to direct court control.

sentences.zh: 河坊非危急泛科、免夫錢並罷。

translations.literal: River wards' non-urgent general levies and corvée exemption fees—all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous river-ward levies and corvée exemption fees were abolished.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 是時天下財用歲入，有御前錢物、朝廷錢物、戶部錢物，其措置裒斂、取索支用，各不相知。

translations.literal: At this time the realm's annual fiscal intake had imperial-front monies, court monies, and Ministry of Revenue monies; their arrangements for collection and disbursement each did not know the other.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue was split among imperial privy funds, court funds, and Ministry of Revenue funds, whose collection and spending were kept separate.

sentences.zh: 天下財賦多為禁中私財，上溢下漏，而民重困。

translations.literal: The realm's wealth and levies mostly became private wealth of the inner palace; overflow above, leakage below—and the people were doubly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the empire's revenue became palace private funds; wealth pooled above while the people bore the cost below.

sentences.zh: 言者請令戶部周知大數，而不失盈虛緩急之宜。

translations.literal: Memorialists asked that the Ministry of Revenue thoroughly know the great totals without losing the balance of surplus, deficit, urgency, and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Critics urged the Ministry of Revenue to oversee aggregate accounts and balance surplus against urgent need.

sentences.zh: 上至宮禁所須，下逮吏卒廩餼，一切付之有司，格以法度，示天下以至公。

translations.literal: From palace needs above down to clerks' and soldiers' rations below—everything paid to the regular offices, framed by law and statutes, showing all under Heaven utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: From palace needs to clerks' rations, all spending was to pass through regular offices under law, demonstrating fairness to the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書聶山亦請以熙、豐後增置添給，如額外醫官、內中諸閣分位次主管文字等使臣、福源靈應諸觀清衛卒、後妃戚裏及文武臣僚之家母妻封國太夫人郡太夫人等請給，並添給食料、茶湯等錢四十萬八千九百餘緡，凡熙、豐無法該載者罷之。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Nie Shan also asked to abolish post-Xining and post-Yuanfeng added stipends—such as extra medical officers, inner-palace clerks for rank-order posts, guards of blessed and numinous temples, stipends for imperial consorts' kin and civil and military officials' mothers and wives as State Madam and Commandery Madam, and added food and tea money totaling four hundred eight thousand nine hundred-odd strings; all not covered by Xining and Yuanfeng law was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Nie Shan also sought to abolish post-reform stipends—extra medical officers, inner-palace clerks, temple guards, stipends for imperial kin and officials' wives with noble titles, and supplemental food and tea allowances totaling over 408,000 strings—anything not authorized under Xining and Yuanfeng law.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔曰：“朕托於兆庶之上，永念民惟邦本，思所以閔恤安定之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict said: "I rest upon the myriad masses above and ever think the people are the state's foundation, seeking how to pity, comfort, and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang year one an edict declared: "Standing above the myriad people, I hold that the people are the foundation of the state and seek ways to pity and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 乃者，減乘輿服禦，放宮女，罷苑囿，焚玩好之物，務以率先天下；

translations.literal: Recently I reduced imperial carriage robes and regalia, released palace women, abolished parks and gardens, burned objects of delight—striving to take the lead for all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: I have reduced imperial regalia, released palace women, abolished parks, and burned luxuries to lead the realm by example;

sentences.zh: 減冗官，澄濫賞，汰貪吏，為民除害。

translations.literal: reduced redundant officials, clarified excessive rewards, eliminated greedy officials—removing harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: cut redundant offices, curbed lavish rewards, and removed corrupt officials to spare the people.

sentences.zh: 方詔減上供收買之額，蠲有司煩苛之令，輕刑薄賦，務安元元；

translations.literal: I was about to reduce court tribute purchase quotas, repeal onerous bureau orders, lighten punishments and thin levies, striving to settle the masses;
translations.idiomatic: I had ordered reduced tribute purchases, repeal of onerous regulations, lighter punishments, and lower taxes to settle the people;

sentences.zh: 而田裏之間，愁痛未蘇，儻不蠲革，何以靖民！

translations.literal: yet between fields and hamlets grief and pain were not yet eased—if we do not broadly reform, how can the people be settled!
translations.idiomatic: yet in the countryside distress had not eased—without broad reform, how can the people be pacified!

sentences.zh: 今詢酌庶言，疏剔眾弊，舉其綱目，以授四方。

translations.literal: Now I have consulted diverse opinions, sifted many abuses, raised their outlines, and entrusted them to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Now, having consulted widely and sifted abuses, I set forth these measures for the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔到，監司、郡守其悉力奉行；

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, supervisory commissioners and prefects and magistrates shall all exert their strength to carry it out;
translations.idiomatic: When this edict arrives, supervisors and prefectural officials must enforce it fully;

sentences.zh: 應民所疾苦，不在此詔，許推類聞奏。

translations.literal: where the people's suffering lies outside this edict, they may report by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: and may report by analogy on hardships not covered here.

sentences.zh: ”於是凡當時苛刻煩細、一切不便於民者皆罷。

translations.literal: Thus all harsh, minute, and inconvenient measures of the time were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every harsh or burdensome measure then troubling the people was abolished.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年，詔：“諸路無額上供錢，依舊法，更不立額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan under Emperor Gaozong, an edict said: "Non-quota court tribute money on all circuits shall follow the old law and no new quota shall be set.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's first Jianyan year an edict ordered: "Non-quota tribute money in every circuit shall follow former law, with no new quotas imposed.

sentences.zh: ”三年二月，減婺州上供額羅二萬八千匹，著為定制。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Wuzhou's quota tribute thin silk was reduced by twenty-eight thousand bolts and fixed as the established rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year three, Wuzhou's tribute quota of thin silk was cut by 28,000 bolts and fixed as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 八月，減福建、廣南路歲買上供銀三分之一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Fujian and Guangnan circuits' annual court-purchase tribute silver was reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, annual tribute silver purchases in Fujian and Guangnan were cut by one-third.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，罷鎮江府禦服羅，省錢七萬緡，助劉光世軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, Zhenjiang prefecture's imperial-robe thin silk was abolished—saving seventy thousand strings to aid Liu Guangshi's army.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year two, Zhenjiang's imperial-robe silk levy was ended, saving 70,000 strings for Liu Guangshi's forces.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，詔：“諸路州縣天申節禮物，並置場和買，毋得抑配於民。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, an edict said: "On all circuits, prefectures, and counties, Tian Shen Festival gifts shall be purchased at fair-market offices and must not be forcibly apportioned on the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, second month, an edict ordered: "Tian Shen Festival gifts must be bought at fair price and not forcibly levied on the people.

sentences.zh: ”十有一月，免淮南州軍大禮絹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Huainan circuits' and armies' great-ritual silk was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, great-ritual silk levies on Huainan circuits and armies were remitted.

sentences.zh: 五年，以四川上供錢帛依舊留以贍軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Sichuan's court tribute money and silks were left as before to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, Sichuan tribute funds and silks were retained locally to support troops.

sentences.zh: 十一年，始命四川上供羅復輸內藏，其後綾、紗、絹悉如之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Sichuan tribute thin silk was first ordered again sent to the inner treasury; afterward twill, gauze, and silk followed suit.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, Sichuan tribute thin silk was again sent to the inner treasury, followed by twill, gauze, and silk.

sentences.zh: （四路天申節大禮絹及上供綢、綾、錦、綺，共九萬五千八百匹。）〉

translations.literal: (Four circuits: Tian Shen Festival great-ritual silk and court tribute figured silk, twill, brocade, and gauze—ninety-five thousand eight hundred bolts in all.) closing mark〉
translations.idiomatic: (Silks for the Tian Shen Festival and court tribute from four circuits—figured silk, twill, brocade, and gauze—totaled 95,800 bolts.) closing mark〉

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，湖北漕臣劉焞言：“鄂、嶽、漢陽自紹興九年所收賦財，十分為率，儲一分充上供始，十三年年增二分。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, Hubei transport commissioner Liu Yun said: "Ezhou, Yuezhou, and Hanyang, from the ninth year of Shaoxing in collected tax wealth, taking ten parts as the rate, stored one part for court tribute at first; from the thirteenth year they increased two parts yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi year five, Hubei transport commissioner Liu Yun reported: "Since Shaoxing year nine, Ezhou, Yuezhou, and Hanyang had set aside one-tenth of tax receipts for court tribute, then raised the reserve by two-tenths each year from year thirteen.

sentences.zh: 鄂州元儲一分，錢一萬九千五百七十緡，今已增至一十二萬九千餘緡；

translations.literal: Ezhou originally stored one part—nineteen thousand five hundred seventy strings; now it has increased to one hundred twenty-nine thousand-odd strings;
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou's reserve had been 19,570 strings and had risen to over 129,000;

sentences.zh: 岳州五千八百餘緡，今增至四萬二千一百餘緡；

translations.literal: Yuezhou five thousand eight hundred-odd strings; now increased to forty-two thousand one hundred-odd strings;
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou's from 5,800 strings to over 42,100;

sentences.zh: 漢陽三千七百緡，今增至二萬二千三百餘緡。

translations.literal: Hanyang three thousand seven hundred strings; now increased to twenty-two thousand three hundred-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: and Hanyang's from 3,700 strings to over 22,300.

sentences.zh: 民力凋弊，無所從出。

translations.literal: The people's strength is withered and exhausted; there is nowhere from which to draw.
translations.idiomatic: The people are exhausted, with no means left to pay.

sentences.zh: ”於是以見增錢數立額，已後權免遞增。

translations.literal: Thereupon the present increased amounts were fixed as quotas; hereafter incremental increases were temporarily exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne fixed quotas at current levels and barred further yearly increases.

sentences.zh: 詔夔州路九州百姓科買上供金、銀、絹，自淳熙六年為始盡免。

translations.literal: An edict exempted the nine prefectures of Kuizhou circuit from levied court tribute gold, silver, and silk, beginning in the sixth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: From Chunxi year six, court tribute levies of gold, silver, and silk were abolished for the nine prefectures of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，蠲兩淮州軍合發上供諸窠名錢物，極邊全免，次邊展免一年。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, all nominal-account court tribute monies and goods for Huai-Hai circuits and armies were remitted; the outermost border fully exempted, the next border granted one year's extension.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen, Huai-Hai tribute levies were remitted entirely on the outer frontier and deferred one year on the next tier.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，江、浙諸州軍折輸上供物帛錢數，除合起輕貨，並用錢、會中半；

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding, for Jiang and Zhe circuits' commuted court tribute goods and cash, apart from light goods due, half was paid in cash and merchant bills;
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding year one, commuted tribute payments in Jiang and Zhe were half paid in cash and merchant notes, except for light goods still due in kind;

sentences.zh: 路不通水，願以銀折輸者聽，兩不過三貫三百文。

translations.literal: where routes lacked waterways, those wishing to pay in silver were permitted—two taels not exceeding three strings three hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: where waterways were unavailable, silver payment was allowed at no more than 3,300 cash per tael.

sentences.zh: 兩浙、江東共四百一十三萬八千六百一十二貫有奇，並輸送左藏西庫。

translations.literal: Liangzhe and Jiangdong together four million one hundred thirty-eight thousand six hundred twelve strings odd—all delivered to the Left Treasury Western Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhe and Jiangdong together delivered over 4.13 million strings to the Left Treasury Western Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳六年，都省言：“南渡以來，諸路上供數重，自嘉定至嘉熙，起截之數雖減，而州縣猶以大數拘催，害及百姓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianchun, the Secretariat said: "Since the southern crossing, circuits' court tribute burdens have been heavy; from Jiading to Jiaxi, though intercepted amounts were reduced, prefectures and counties still pressed collection on the great quota, harming the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun year six the Secretariat reported: "Since the southern crossing, tribute burdens had grown; though intercepted quotas fell from Jiading to Jiaxi, counties still collected at old high figures and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: ”有旨：“自鹹淳七年為始，銀、錢、關、會用鹹淳三年起截中數拘催，綢、絹、絲、綿、綾、羅用鹹淳二年起截中數拘催。

translations.literal: An order said: "From the seventh year of Xianchun onward, silver, cash, merchant bills, and paper notes shall be collected at the mid-level intercepted quota from Xianchun year three; figured silk, silk, raw silk, cotton, twill, and gauze at the mid-level from Xianchun year two.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered that from Xianchun year seven, cash and silver collections follow the year-three intercepted median, and silk goods the year-two median.

sentences.zh: 錢、關、會子二千四百九十五萬八千七百四十八貫，銀一十六萬九千六百四十三兩，綢四萬一千四百三十八匹，絹七十三萬七千八百六十匹，絲九萬五千三百三十三兩，綿一百五萬七千九百二十五兩，綾五千一百七十九匹，羅七千三百五十五匹，戶部遍牒諸路，視今所減定額起催。

translations.literal: Cash, merchant bills, and paper notes two billion four hundred ninety-five million eight hundred seventy-eight thousand seven hundred forty-eight strings; silver one hundred sixty-nine thousand six hundred forty-three taels; figured silk forty-one thousand four hundred thirty-eight bolts; silk seven hundred thirty-seven thousand eight hundred sixty bolts; raw silk ninety-five thousand three hundred thirty-three taels; cotton one million five hundred seventy-nine thousand nine hundred twenty-five taels; twill five thousand one hundred seventy-nine bolts; gauze seven thousand three hundred fifty-five bolts—the Ministry of Revenue issued circulars to all circuits to collect according to these reduced fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Totals were set at 2.49 billion strings in cash and notes, 169,643 taels of silver, and specified silk quantities; the Ministry of Revenue ordered every circuit to collect only at these reduced quotas.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 所謂經總製錢者，宣和末，陳亨伯以發運兼經製使，因以為名。

translations.literal: What is called comprehensive fiscal reserve money: at the end of Xuanhe, Chen Hengbo, as transport commissioner concurrently comprehensive fiscal commissioner, took this as the name.
translations.idiomatic: The comprehensive fiscal reserve funds originated when Chen Hengbo, as transport commissioner and comprehensive fiscal commissioner at the end of Xuanhe, gave them that name.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，高宗在揚州，四方貢賦不以期至，戶部尚書呂頤浩、翰林學士葉夢得等言：“亨伯以東南用兵，嚐設經製司，取量添酒錢及增一分稅錢，頭子、賣契等錢，斂之於細，而積之甚眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong was at Yangzhou; tribute from the four quarters did not arrive on schedule. Minister of Revenue Lü Yihao, Hanlin academician Ye Mengde, and others said: "Hengbo, because the southeast used troops, once set up a comprehensive fiscal office, taking added wine tax and an added one-percent tax, head-money, deed-sale money, and the like—levying in small amounts yet accumulating very many.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan year two, with Gaozong at Yangzhou and revenues delayed, Lü Yihao and Ye Mengde recalled how Hengbo had created a comprehensive fiscal office during southeastern campaigns, levying small surcharges—added wine tax, a one-percent levy, head-money, deed taxes—that accumulated vast sums.

sentences.zh: 及為河北轉運使，又行於京東西、河北路，一歲得錢近二百萬緡，所補不細。

translations.literal: When he became Hebei transport commissioner, he extended it to Jingdong, Jingxi, and Hebei circuits; in one year he obtained nearly two million strings—the supplement was not slight.
translations.idiomatic: As Hebei transport commissioner he extended the system east and north, raising nearly two million strings in a year.

sentences.zh: 今若行於諸路州軍，歲入無慮數百萬計。

translations.literal: If it is now carried out in prefectures and counties on all circuits, yearly intake will be several million without concern.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to every prefecture and county, annual intake could reach hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 邊事未寧，苟不出此，緩急必致暴斂。

translations.literal: Border affairs are not yet settled; if this is not done, in urgency one will surely resort to harsh levies.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier unsettled, without this measure emergencies would force harsh exactions.

sentences.zh: 與其斂於倉卒，曷若積於細微。

translations.literal: Rather than levy in emergency, how much better to accumulate in minute amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Far better to gather revenue in small steady streams than to seize it in a crisis.

sentences.zh: ”於是以添酒錢、添賣糟錢、典賣田宅增牙稅錢、官員等請給頭子錢、樓店務增三分房錢，令兩浙、江東西、荊湖南北、福建、二廣收充經製錢，以憲臣領之，通判斂之，季終輸送。

translations.literal: Thereupon added wine tax, added distillery-sale tax, added deed tax on sold fields and houses, head-money on officials' stipends, and a three-percent increase on shop-office rents were ordered collected in Liangzhe, Jiangdong, Jiangxi, Jinghu, Fujian, and the two Guang circuits as comprehensive fiscal reserve money, led by surveillance commissioners, collected by vice-prefects, and delivered quarterly.
translations.idiomatic: Added wine taxes, distillery-sale surcharges, property deed taxes, stipend head-money, and a three-percent shop rent increase were then levied across the southeast and south as comprehensive fiscal reserve funds, overseen by surveillance commissioners, collected by vice-prefects, and remitted quarterly.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，參政孟庾提領措置財用，請以總製司為名，又因經製之額增析而為總製錢，而總製錢自此始矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Participating Administrator Meng Geng, overseeing fiscal arrangements, asked that the office be named the General Fiscal Bureau; on the comprehensive fiscal quota it further divided general comprehensive money—and general comprehensive money began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year five, Meng Geng, overseeing fiscal policy, renamed the office the General Fiscal Bureau and split a further general comprehensive fund from the comprehensive quota—thus general comprehensive funds began.

sentences.zh: 財用司言：“諸路州縣出納係省錢所收頭子錢，貫收錢二十三文省，內一十文省作經製起發上供，餘一十三文充本路郡縣並漕司用。

translations.literal: The Fiscal Affairs Bureau said: "On head-money collected from provincial treasury receipts in prefectures and counties on all circuits, per string twenty-three cash provincial was received; within it ten cash provincial was sent as comprehensive fiscal reserve for court tribute, the remaining thirteen cash supplied the circuit, counties, and transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiscal Affairs Bureau reported that of the twenty-three cash head-money per string on provincial receipts, ten had funded comprehensive reserves for court tribute and thirteen had gone to circuits, counties, and transport offices.

sentences.zh: 今欲令諸路州縣雜稅出納錢貫收頭子錢上，量增作二十三文足。

translations.literal: Now it is desired that on miscellaneous tax receipts in prefectures and counties on all circuits, head-money per string be increased in measure to twenty-three cash full.
translations.idiomatic: It proposed raising head-money on all miscellaneous tax receipts to twenty-three cash per string in full measure.

sentences.zh: 除漕司及州舊合得一十三文省，餘盡入經製窠名帳內，起發助軍。

translations.literal: Apart from the transport commission and prefectures' old thirteen cash provincial, the remainder all enters comprehensive fiscal nominal accounts and is sent to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the thirteen cash retained locally, the remainder would enter comprehensive fiscal accounts to support the army.

sentences.zh: ”江西提舉司言：“常平錢物，舊法貫收頭子錢五文足。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi Intendant Office said: "Ever-normal granary monies—by old law five cash full per string was collected as head-money.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi Intendant Office noted that ever-normal granary funds had formerly charged five cash head-money per string.

sentences.zh: 今當依諸色錢例，增作二十三文足，除五文依舊法支用，餘增到錢與經製司別作窠名輸送。

translations.literal: Now it should follow the rule for all monies, increased to twenty-three cash full; apart from five cash used by old law, the remainder of the increase is remitted to the comprehensive fiscal office under a separate nominal account.
translations.idiomatic: It asked that granary receipts follow the new rule of twenty-three cash, retaining five cash under old law and remitting the increase to comprehensive fiscal accounts.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 九年，諫議大夫曾統上疏言：“經製使本戶部之職，更置一司，無益於事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Zeng Tong submitted a memorial saying: "The comprehensive fiscal commissioner is originally the Ministry of Revenue's duty; establishing another office does not benefit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, Remonstrance Adviser Zeng Tong memorialized: "Comprehensive fiscal oversight belongs to the Ministry of Revenue; a separate office serves no purpose.

sentences.zh: 如創供給酒庫，亦是陰奪省司之利。

translations.literal: Such as newly supplying wine warehouses—it also secretly seizes the provincial office's profit.
translations.idiomatic: Creating supply wine warehouses merely steals revenue from regular agencies.

sentences.zh: 若謂監司、郡縣違法廢令，別建此司按之，則又不然。

translations.literal: If one says surveillance commissioners and prefectures and counties violate law and abolish orders, and this office is separately established to investigate them, that too is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Nor would a separate inspectorate truly curb illegal spending by supervisors and counties.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷置監司以轄州郡，立省部以轄監司，祖宗製也。

translations.literal: The court establishes surveillance commissioners to rule prefectures and counties, and provincial departments to rule surveillance commissioners—the forefathers' system.
translations.idiomatic: The court appoints circuit supervisors over prefectures and provincial ministries over supervisors—such was the ancestral system.

sentences.zh: 稅賦失實，當問轉運司；

translations.literal: If tax levies miss reality, one should question the transport commission;
translations.idiomatic: False tax returns belong to the transport commission;

sentences.zh: 常平錢穀失陷，當問提舉司。

translations.literal: if ever-normal grain and money are lost or sunk, one should question the intendant office.
translations.idiomatic: and lost ever-normal funds to the intendant office.

sentences.zh: 若使經製司能事事檢察，則雖戶部版曹，亦可廢矣。

translations.literal: If the comprehensive fiscal office can inspect everything, then even the Ministry of Revenue's ledger bureau could be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: If the comprehensive fiscal office could inspect everything, the Ministry's own ledger bureau might as well be abolished.

sentences.zh: 且自置司以來，漕司之移用，憲司之贓罰，監司之妄支，固未嚐少革其弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the office was established, transport commissions' diversions, surveillance commissioners' penal forfeitures, and supervisory commissioners' reckless disbursements have indeed not been slightly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Since its founding, transport diversions, surveillance penalties, and supervisory abuses had scarcely improved.

sentences.zh: 罷之便。

translations.literal: Abolishing it would be expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Abolition would be the better course.

sentences.zh: ”疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以諸路歲取經總製錢，本路提刑並檢法幹辦官拘催，歲終通紐以課殿最。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for annual collection of general comprehensive fiscal reserve money on all circuits, the circuit judicial intendant together with legal-inspection executive officers were charged to press collection; at year's end aggregate reconciliation was used to assess merit rankings.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen, circuit judicial intendants and legal-inspection officers were ordered to press annual collection of general comprehensive reserve funds, with year-end totals reconciled for merit rankings.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以守、倅同檢察。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, prefects and vice-prefects jointly inspected.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one, prefects and their deputies shared oversight.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔專以通判主之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict designated supervising vice-prefects to administer it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine, an edict put collection solely in the hands of supervising vice-prefects.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，詔：“諸路州縣出納，貫添收錢一十三文省，充經總製錢，以所增錢別輸左藏西庫，補助經費。

translations.literal: Qiandao year 1, edict: "On receipts and disbursements in prefectures and counties on all circuits, add thirteen cash provincial per string collected as general comprehensive fiscal reserve money; remit the added amount separately to the Left Treasury western depot to supplement fiscal expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao year one, the court ordered that every string of prefectural receipts include thirteen cash provincial for general comprehensive reserves, with the surcharge remitted to the Left Treasury western depot to supplement routine expenses.

sentences.zh: ”自是經總製錢每千收五十六文矣。

translations.literal: "From thence general comprehensive fiscal reserve money collected fifty-six cash per thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the general comprehensive reserve levy stood at fifty-six cash per thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 然遇兵凶，亦時有蠲免。

translations.literal: Yet when warfare and disaster struck, exemptions were sometimes granted.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, wartime and disaster sometimes brought partial remissions.

sentences.zh: 三年，復以守、倅共掌之。

translations.literal: In year three, prefects and vice-prefects again jointly administered it.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, prefects and deputies again shared administration.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年，光宗即位，減江東西、福建、淮東、浙西經總製錢一十七萬一千緡。

translations.literal: Chunxi year 16, when Guangzong succeeded, reduced general comprehensive fiscal reserve money in Jiangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Huaidong, and Zhexi by 171,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong succeeded in Chunxi year sixteen, general comprehensive reserves in the southeast circuits were cut by 171,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，詔平江府合發經總製錢歲減二萬緡。

translations.literal: Shaoxi year 2, edict reduced Pingjiang prefecture's combined annual general comprehensive fiscal remittance by 20,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi year two, Pingjiang's annual comprehensive reserve quota was lowered by 20,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十七年，詔蠲嘉定十五年終以前所虧錢數。

translations.literal: Jiading year 17, edict remitted the amount of money shortfalls through the end of Jiading year 15.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year seventeen, the court wrote off deficits accumulated through the end of Jiading year fifteen.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，詔：“諸路州軍因災傷檢放苗米，毋收經總製頭子、勘合朱墨等錢；

translations.literal: Duanping year 3, edict: "Where prefectures on all circuits inspect and release seed-grain tax rice because of disaster injury, do not collect general comprehensive reserve head-money, verification ink fees, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: In Duanping year three, the court ruled that where disaster relief released seed-grain tax rice, circuits must not charge comprehensive reserve head-money, verification fees, or similar surcharges;

sentences.zh: 自今已放苗米，隨苗帶納錢並與除放。

translations.literal: where seed-grain tax rice has already been released, grain-tied ancillary payments are likewise remitted.
translations.idiomatic: and that grain-tied surcharges already remitted with released seed tax should also be forgiven.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 所謂月樁錢者，始於紹興之二年。

translations.literal: What is called monthly quota money began in the second year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly quota funds dated from Shaoxing year two.

sentences.zh: 時韓世忠駐軍建康，宰相呂頤浩、朱勝非議今江東漕臣月樁發大軍錢十萬緡，以朝廷上供經製及漕司移用等錢供億。

translations.literal: At that time Han Shizhong's army was stationed at Jiankang; Grand Councillors Lü Yihao and Zhu Shengfei proposed that the Jiangdong transport commissioner monthly quota 100,000 strings for the grand army, supplied from court tribute for comprehensive fiscal arrangements and transport commission diverted funds.
translations.idiomatic: With Han Shizhong's forces at Jiankang, Grand Councillors Lü Yihao and Zhu Shengfei urged the Jiangdong transport commissioner to advance 100,000 strings monthly for the main army, drawn from court tribute, comprehensive fiscal quotas, and transport diversions.

sentences.zh: 當時漕司不量州軍之力，一例均科，既有偏重之弊，

translations.literal: Then transport commissioners did not measure prefectures' capacity but levied uniformly in one rule, already having the abuse of disproportionate burden,
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners ignored local capacity and imposed flat quotas, which already bore unfairly on weaker prefectures,

sentences.zh: （上供經製，無額添酒錢並爭利錢，贍軍酒息錢，常平錢，及諸司封樁不封樁、係省不係省錢，皆是朝廷窠名也。）〉

translations.literal: (Court tribute for comprehensive fiscal arrangements, unquota added wine tax and competitive-profit tax, army-support wine interest tax, ever-normal funds, and all offices' sealed and unsealed, provincial and non-provincial monies—all are court nominal accounts.)
translations.idiomatic: (Court tribute for comprehensive fiscal arrangements, discretionary wine surcharges, competitive-profit levies, army-support wine interest, ever-normal funds, and every sealed or unsealed, provincial or non-provincial account—all belonged to the court's nominal revenue schedule.)

sentences.zh: 於是郡縣橫斂，銖積絲累，江東、西之害尤甚。

translations.literal: then prefectures and counties levied harshly, penny by penny piled up; Jiangdong and Jiangxi suffered especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties then extorted layer upon layer of petty levies, with Jiangdong and Jiangxi hardest hit.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔州郡以寬剩錢充月樁，以寬民力，遂減江東、西之錢二十七萬七千緡有奇。

translations.literal: Year seventeen, edict ordered prefectures to supply monthly quota from surplus funds to ease the people, thereby reducing Jiangdong and Jiangxi money by 277,000-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, prefectures were told to meet monthly quotas from surplus funds to ease the populace, cutting Jiangdong and Jiangxi quotas by more than 277,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 又有所謂板帳錢者，亦軍興後所創也。

translations.literal: There was also what was called ledger-account money, likewise created after the military emergency.
translations.idiomatic: A parallel category called ledger-account funds likewise arose after the wars began.

sentences.zh: 如輸米則增收耗剩，交錢帛則多收糜費，幸富人之犯法而重其罰，恣胥吏之受賕而課其入，索盜贓則不償失主，檢財產則不及卑幼，亡僧、絕戶不俟核實而入官，逃產、廢田不與消除而抑納，他如此類，不可遍舉。
