translations.literal: For example, on rice delivered extra surplus was collected; on silk and cash handed over extra wastage fees were taken; the wealthy were fortunate to violate law so penalties could be doubled; clerks were indulged in bribes so intake could be assessed; stolen goods were seized without compensating owners; property inspections did not reach junior kin; deceased monks and extinct households were entered to the state without awaiting verification; abandoned fields and forfeited estates were not struck from rolls but still assessed—other cases of this kind cannot all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: Deliveries of rice drew surplus charges; payments in cash or silk drew inflated handling fees; officials welcomed rich lawbreakers because fines swelled revenue; clerks were encouraged to take bribes counted as quota; stolen goods were confiscated without restitution; estate surveys skipped junior heirs; dead monks and heirless households were seized before verification; abandoned land stayed on the tax rolls—examples multiplied beyond count.

sentences.zh: 州縣之吏固知其非法，然以版帳錢額太重，雖欲不橫取於民，不可得已。

translations.literal: Prefectural clerks indeed knew these were illegal, yet because ledger-account quotas were too heavy, even if they wished not to levy harshly on the people, they could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials knew the practice was unlawful, but ledger-account targets were so high that they could not refrain from extortion even when they wished to.

sentences.zh: 凡貨財不領於有司者，則有內藏庫，蓋天子之別藏也。

translations.literal: For goods and wealth not held by regular offices, there was the inner treasury—essentially the Son of Heaven's separate storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth kept outside regular agencies belonged to the inner treasury, the emperor's private reserve.

sentences.zh: 縣官有钜費，左藏之積不足給，則發內藏佐之。

translations.literal: When the state had great expenses and Left Treasury accumulations were insufficient, the inner treasury supplemented them.
translations.idiomatic: When routine revenues fell short of major state costs, the inner treasury made up the gap.

sentences.zh: 宋初，諸州貢賦皆輸左藏庫，及取荊湖，定巴蜀，平嶺南、江南，諸國珍寶、金帛盡入內府。

translations.literal: Early in the Song, all circuit tribute was sent to the Left Treasury; after taking Jinghu, settling Bashu, and pacifying Lingnan and Jiangnan, the various states' treasures and gold and silk all entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song tribute flowed to the Left Treasury; conquests in Jinghu, Sichuan, Lingnan, and the lower Yangzi then filled the inner palace with regional treasures.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以帑藏盈溢，又於講武殿後別為內庫，嚐謂：“軍旅、饑饉當預為之備，不可臨事厚斂於民。

translations.literal: Initially, because the vaults overflowed, Taizu also established a separate inner depot behind the Lecture on Warfare Hall, once saying: "For campaigns and famine one should prepare in advance and must not, when events arise, levy heavily on the people.
translations.idiomatic: When state vaults overflowed, Taizu added a second inner depot behind the Lecture on Warfare Hall, remarking that armies and famine should be met from stockpiles, not from sudden heavy levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，漳泉、吳越相次獻地，又下太原，儲積益厚，分左藏庫為內藏庫，令內藏庫使翟裔等於左藏庫擇上綾羅等物別造帳籍，月申樞密院；

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded, Zhang-Quan and Wuyue in turn submitted territory and Taiyuan was taken; stores grew thicker; the Left Treasury was divided into an inner treasury, and Inner Treasury Commissioner Zhai Yi and others at the Left Treasury selected superior damask and gauze and the like and made separate ledgers, monthly reporting to the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's reign brought Zhang-Quan, Wuyue, and Taiyuan into the empire and swelled reserves; he split the Left Treasury, had Commissioner Zhai Yi catalog choice silks in separate ledgers reported monthly to the Bureau of Military Affairs,

sentences.zh: 改講武殿後庫為景福殿庫，俾隸內藏。

translations.literal: the depot behind Lecture on Warfare Hall was renamed the Jingfu Hall depot and made subordinate to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: and renamed the rear depot the Jingfu Hall store under inner-treasury control.

sentences.zh: 其後乃令揀納諸州上供物，具月帳於內東門進入，外庭不得預其事。

translations.literal: Later he ordered selection and intake of tribute goods from all prefectures, with monthly accounts submitted through the inner east gate; the outer court could not participate in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later, selected tribute from every prefecture was logged monthly through the inner east gate, beyond outer-court scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 帝因謂左右曰：“此蓋慮司計之臣不能節約，異時用度有闕，復賦率於民，朕不以此自供嗜好也。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore told those around him: "This is because I fear fiscal officers cannot be frugal; if someday expenditures fall short, they will again levy on the people—I do not use this to supply my own tastes.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants that the reserve guarded against spendthrift fiscal officers who might otherwise re-levy the people in a crisis—not to indulge his personal tastes.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 自乾德、開寶以來，用兵及水旱振給、慶澤賜賚、有司計度之所闕者，必籍其數以貸於內藏，候課賦有餘，即償之。

translations.literal: From Qiande and Kaibao onward, whenever campaigns, flood and drought relief, celebratory grants, or agency shortfalls in planning required funds, the amount was always recorded and borrowed from the inner treasury; when tax revenues had surplus, it was repaid.
translations.idiomatic: From Qiande and Kaibao on, wars, disaster relief, ceremonial grants, and agency deficits were covered by recorded loans from the inner treasury, repaid when tax revenues allowed.

sentences.zh: 淳化後二十五年間，歲貸百萬，有至三百萬者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-five years after Chunhua, yearly loans reached one million strings, sometimes three million.
translations.idiomatic: Over the twenty-five years after Chunhua, annual loans ran to one million strings and sometimes three million.

sentences.zh: 累歲不能償，則除其籍。

translations.literal: When years passed without repayment, the record was struck from the books.
translations.idiomatic: Long-unpaid debts were simply written off.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，又以新衣庫為內藏西庫。

translations.literal: Jingde year 4, the New Garments Depot was also made the inner treasury western depot.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde year four, the New Garments Depot became the inner treasury's western wing.

sentences.zh: 初，劉承珪嚐掌庫，經製多其所置，又推究置庫以來出納，造都帳及《須知》，屢加賞焉。

translations.literal: Initially Liu Chenggui had managed the depot; many regulations were of his making, and he also traced receipts and disbursements since the depot's founding, producing a master ledger and the 《Essentials to Know》, and was repeatedly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chenggui, who had long managed the depot, shaped many of its rules, reconstructed its ledgers since founding, compiled the 《Essentials to Know》, and won repeated rewards.

sentences.zh: 真宗再臨幸，作銘刻石。

translations.literal: Zhenzong visited twice and had an inscription carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong visited twice and ordered a stone inscription.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，重修庫屋，增廣其地。

translations.literal: Dazhong Xiangfu year 5, the depot buildings were rebuilt and the grounds expanded.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu year five, the depot was rebuilt and enlarged.

sentences.zh: 既而又以香藥庫、儀鸞司屋益之，分為四庫：金銀一庫，珠玉、香藥一庫，錦帛一庫，錢一庫。

translations.literal: Later the aromatics depot and Palace Ceremonial Office buildings were added, divided into four depots: gold and silver; pearls, jade, and aromatics; brocades and silks; and cash.
translations.idiomatic: Aromatics stores and ceremonial offices were later annexed, dividing holdings into gold and silver, gems and aromatics, silks, and coin.

sentences.zh: 金銀、珠寶有十色，錢有新舊二色，錦帛十三色，香藥七色。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, and gems had ten grades; cash had new and old types; brocades and silks thirteen grades; aromatics seven grades.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures were sorted into ten grades of metal and gems, two coin types, thirteen silk grades, and seven aromatics grades.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，又出內藏緡錢二百萬給三司。

translations.literal: Tianxi year 2, 2,000,000 strings from the inner treasury were again given to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi year two, two million strings were again released to the Three Departments Commission.

sentences.zh: 天聖以後，兵師、水旱費無常數，三歲一賚軍士，出錢百萬緡，綢絹百萬匹，銀三十萬兩，錦綺、鹿胎、透背、綾羅紗縠合五十萬匹，以佐三司。

translations.literal: After Tiansheng, military and flood expenses had no fixed sum; every three years soldiers were rewarded, disbursing one million strings, one million bolts of silk, 300,000 taels of silver, and fifty thousand bolts combined of brocade, deer-fetus weave, openwork backing, gauze, and thin silk to assist the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After Tiansheng, military and disaster costs grew unpredictable; triennial troop rewards sent the Three Departments one million strings, a million bolts of silk, 300,000 taels of silver, and fifty thousand bolts of brocades and gauzes.

sentences.zh: 又歲入饒、池、江、建新鑄緡錢一百七萬，而斥舊蓄緡錢六十萬於左藏庫，率以為常。

translations.literal: Each year newly cast strings from Rao, Chi, Jiang, and Jian totaled 1,070,000, while 600,000 old stored strings were sent out to the Left Treasury—this became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Annual new coin from Rao, Chi, Jiang, and Jian mints reached 1,070,000 strings, while 600,000 older strings were transferred to the Left Treasury as standing practice.

sentences.zh: 異時三司用度不足，必請貸於內藏，輒得之，其名為貸，實罕能償。

translations.literal: When the Three Departments' expenditures were insufficient, they always requested loans from the inner treasury and always received them; though called loans, repayment was rare.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Three Departments ran short, they borrowed from the inner treasury and almost always got the funds—loans in name, seldom repaid in fact.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，內藏庫主者言：“歲斥緡錢六十萬助三司，自天禧三年始。

translations.literal: In Jingyou, the inner treasury director said: "Each year 600,000 strings are disbursed to aid the Three Departments, beginning in Tianxi year 3.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou, the inner treasury director reported that 600,000 strings yearly had aided the Three Departments since Tianxi year three,

sentences.zh: 計明道二年距今才四年，而所貸錢帛九百一十七萬。

translations.literal: Counting from Mingdao year 2 to now is only four years, yet money and silk loaned totals 9,170,000.
translations.idiomatic: yet in only four years since Mingdao year two loans had reached 9,170,000.

sentences.zh: ”在太宗時三司所貸甚眾，久不能償，至慶曆中，詔悉蠲之。

translations.literal: "Under Taizong the Three Departments borrowed heavily and long could not repay; by Qingli an edict remitted all.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong-era Three Departments debts had likewise piled up until Qingli, when the court forgave them entirely.

sentences.zh: 蓋內藏歲入金帛，皇祐中，二百六十五萬七千一十一；

translations.literal: Inner treasury yearly intake in gold and silk: in Huangyou, 2,657,011;
translations.idiomatic: Annual inner-treasury intake in gold and silk reached 2,657,011 in Huangyou;

sentences.zh: 治平一百九十三萬三千五百五十四。

translations.literal: in Zhiping, 1,933,554.
translations.idiomatic: in Zhiping it stood at 1,933,554.

sentences.zh: 其出以助經費，前後不可勝數，至於儲積贏縮，則有司莫得詳焉。

translations.literal: Disbursements to aid routine expenses before and after cannot be numbered; as for whether stores gained or lost, regular offices could not know in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Subsidies to routine budgets were countless, and no agency could fully track whether reserves grew or shrank.

sentences.zh: 神宗臨禦之初，詔立歲輸內藏錢帛之額，視慶曆上供為數。

translations.literal: At the start of Shenzong's reign, an edict fixed the yearly quota of money and silk sent to the inner treasury, taking Qingli tribute as the figure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, the court set annual inner-treasury remittances at Qingli tribute levels.

sentences.zh: 嚐謂輔臣曰：“比閱內藏庫籍，文具而已，財貨出入，初無關防。

translations.literal: He once told chief ministers: "Recently reviewing inner treasury registers, they are documents only; goods in and out initially had no controls.
translations.idiomatic: He told his chief ministers that inner-treasury ledgers were mere paperwork with no real controls on movement of goods.

sentences.zh: 舊以龍腦、珍珠鬻於榷貨務，數年不輸直，亦不鉤考。

translations.literal: Formerly dragon-brain and pearls were sold to the Monopoly Trade Office; for years payment was not delivered, nor was it audited.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-brain and pearls had been sold to the Monopoly Trade Office for years without payment or audit.

sentences.zh: 嚐聞太宗時內藏財庫，每千計用一牙錢記之。

translations.literal: I once heard that in Taizong's time the inner treasury, for every thousand counted, used one tooth coin to record it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, he recalled, had marked every thousand-string lot with a distinctive token coin.

sentences.zh: 凡名物不同，所用錢色亦異，他人莫能曉，匣而置之禦閣，以參驗帳籍中定數。

translations.literal: Whenever names of things differed, the coin color used also differed; others could not understand; they were boxed and placed in the imperial pavilion to verify fixed numbers in the ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: Each commodity type had its own token, kept sealed in the imperial pavilion to cross-check ledger totals outsiders could not read.

sentences.zh: 晚年，出其錢示真宗曰：‘善保此足矣。

translations.literal: In his later years he took out the coins and showed Zhenzong, saying: "Keep this well and it will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he showed Zhenzong those tokens, saying, "Guard these and you will have enough."

sentences.zh: ’今守藏內臣，皆不曉帳籍關防之法。

translations.literal: 'Today the eunuchs who guard the storehouses all do not understand ledger control methods.
translations.idiomatic: Today's storehouse eunuchs no longer understand those ledger controls."

sentences.zh: ”即命幹當禦藥李舜舉領其事。

translations.literal: "He immediately ordered Palace Medicines Superintendent Li Shunju to take charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately put Palace Medicines Superintendent Li Shunju in charge of reform.

sentences.zh: 繼詔諸路金銀輸內藏庫者，歲以帳上三司拘催。

translations.literal: An edict followed that gold and silver sent to the inner treasury from all circuits yearly had accounts submitted and the Three Departments pressed collection.
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up edict required circuit gold and silver remitted to the inner treasury to be logged and collected under Three Departments supervision.

sentences.zh: 元豐以來，又詔諸路金帛、緡錢輸內庫者，委提點刑獄司督趣，若三司、發運司擅留者，坐之。

translations.literal: From Yuanfeng onward, edicts also charged judicial intendants on all circuits to urge gold, silk, and strings sent to the inner depot; if the Three Departments or Transport Commission retained them without authority, they were punished.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanfeng on, judicial intendants supervised gold, silk, and cash bound for the inner depot, punishing the Three Departments or transport offices that withheld remittances.

sentences.zh: 超發坊場錢勿寄市易務，直赴內藏庫寄帳封樁。

translations.literal: Surplus monopoly-shop funds must not be deposited with the Market Exchange Office but sent directly to the inner treasury for sealed-ledger deposit.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus monopoly-shop revenue was to bypass the Market Exchange Office and go straight to inner-treasury sealed accounts.

sentences.zh: 當輸內庫金帛、緡錢，逾期或他用者，如擅用封樁錢法。

translations.literal: Gold, silk, and strings due to the inner depot that were overdue or used for other purposes were treated like unauthorized use of sealed-ledger funds.
translations.idiomatic: Late or diverted inner-depot remittances were penalized like misuse of sealed-ledger funds.

sentences.zh: 初，藝祖嚐欲積縑帛二百萬易敵人首，又別儲於景福殿。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizu once wished to amass two million bolts of silk to buy enemy heads, and also stored separately at the Jingfu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had once hoped to stock two million bolts of silk to ransom enemy heads and kept a separate Jingfu Hall reserve for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，乃更景福殿庫名，自製詩以揭之曰：“五季失圖，玁狁孔熾，藝祖造邦，思有懲艾，爰設內府，基以募士，曾孫保之，敢忘厥誌。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanfeng the Jingfu Hall depot was renamed; he himself composed a poem to display it: "The Five Dynasties lost the map; the Xiongnu grew fierce; Taizu founded the realm, thinking to chasten them; therefore he set the inner depot, basing it on recruiting soldiers; may descendants guard it and not forget the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng the Jingfu depot was renamed and inscribed with his verse: "When the Five Dynasties lost the realm and border foes grew bold, Taizu founded the state and built the inner depot to recruit soldiers—may heirs guard it and never forget that aim."

sentences.zh: ”一字一庫以號之，凡三十二庫。

translations.literal: "One character, one depot as its designation—thirty-two depots in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each character of the poem named a depot, thirty-two in all.

sentences.zh: 後積羨贏為二十庫，又揭詩曰：“每虔夕惕心，妄意遵遺業，顧予不武姿，何日成戎捷。

translations.literal: Later accumulated surplus became twenty depots, and another poem was displayed: "Each evening I reverently examine my heart, daring to think I follow the legacy; considering my unmartial bearing, on what day will martial success be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: As surpluses grew, twenty depots were added under a second verse lamenting his own lack of martial success.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，詔：“祖宗置內藏庫貯經費餘財，所以募士威敵，振乏固本，皆有成法。

translations.literal: Chongning year 1, edict: "The forefathers established the inner treasury to store surplus fiscal wealth, to recruit soldiers and awe enemies, relieve want and strengthen the root—all have established laws.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning year one, the court reminded officials that the inner treasury was meant to stock surplus revenue for troops, enemies, and emergencies under fixed rules.

sentences.zh: 比歲官司懈馳，侵蠹耗減，務在協力遵守，無令偏廢。

translations.literal: In recent years offices have been lax, encroaching and wasting and diminishing; strive together to observe, and do not let any part fall into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: Recent laxity had eroded those reserves, and every office was ordered to uphold the old rules without neglect.

sentences.zh: ”於是命倉部郎中丘括行諸路驅磨。

translations.literal: "Thereupon Revenue Section Director Qiu Kuo was ordered to conduct circuit-wide audits.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Section Director Qiu Kuo was then sent to audit the circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年，中書奏：“熙寧之製，江南諸路金銀課利並輸內帑。

translations.literal: Year three, the Secretariat memorialized: "Under the Xining system, gold and silver profits on Jiangnan circuits all went to the inner vault.
translations.idiomatic: In year three the Secretariat reported that under Xining reforms, Jiangnan gold and silver profits had all flowed to the inner vault.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，戶部尚書李常於中以三分助轉運司，致內帑漸以虧減。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou period, Revenue Minister Li Chang diverted three-tenths to transport commissions, causing the inner vault gradually to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanyou, Revenue Minister Li Chang diverted thirty percent to transport offices, steadily draining the inner vault.

sentences.zh: ”乃詔諸路新舊坑冶所收課利金銀並輸內帑，如熙寧之舊。

translations.literal: "An edict then ordered gold and silver profits from old and new mines on all circuits sent to the inner vault, as under Xining.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored the Xining rule sending all mine profits to the inner vault.

sentences.zh: 後又入於大觀東庫。

translations.literal: Later they again entered the Daguan eastern depot.
translations.idiomatic: Later receipts were routed to the Daguan eastern depot instead.

sentences.zh: 尋命仍舊以七分輸內帑，餘給轉運司。

translations.literal: Soon an order restored the old rule: seven-tenths to the inner vault, the remainder to transport commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the split returned to seventy percent for the inner vault and thirty for transport.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，申截留、借兌內帑錢物之製。

translations.literal: Xuanhe year 6, regulations on withholding and swapping inner-vault goods were tightened.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe year six, rules against withholding or swapping inner-vault goods were reinforced.

sentences.zh: 時又有元豐庫，則雜儲諸司羨餘錢。

translations.literal: At that time there was also the Yuanfeng depot, which miscellaneously stored surplus funds from various offices.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Yuanfeng depot, holding miscellaneous surpluses from government agencies.

sentences.zh: 諸道榷酤場，舊以守衙前之陪備官費者，熙寧役法行，乃聽民增直以售，取其價給衙前。

translations.literal: On monopoly liquor shops on all circuits, formerly guard and yamen runners' attendant costs were supplied; when the Xining corvée law was implemented, commoners were allowed to add price to purchase, and the price was given to yamen runners.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly shops had once funded yamen runners' expenses; under Xining corvée reform, civilians could buy franchises at premium prices that paid those runners.

sentences.zh: 久之，坊場錢益多，司農請歲發百萬緡輸中都。

translations.literal: After long time, monopoly-shop money grew ever greater; the Agriculture Commission requested sending one million strings yearly to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Over time franchise revenues swelled until the Agriculture Commission sought to send one million strings yearly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，遂於司農寺南作元豐庫貯之，以待非常之用。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng year 3, the Yuanfeng depot was built south of the Agriculture Commission to store it, awaiting extraordinary use.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng year three, the Yuanfeng depot was built south of the Agriculture Commission to hold those emergency funds.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，右司諫蘇轍論河北保甲之害，因言：“元豐及內庫財物山委，皆先帝多方蓄藏，以備緩急。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 1, Right Remonstrance Su Zhe, discussing harm from Hebei baojia militia, also said: "Yuanfeng and inner-depot wealth pile mountain-high—all stored by the late emperor against emergency.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou year one, Remonstrance Officer Su Zhe, criticizing Hebei baojia militia, urged using Yuanfeng and inner-depot hoards Taizu had amassed for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 若積而不用，與東漢西園錢，唐之瓊林、大盈二庫何異？

translations.literal: If accumulated yet unused, how does it differ from Eastern Han's Western Garden money or Tang's Qionlin and Daying depots?
translations.idiomatic: Idle hoards, he argued, would repeat the useless Western Garden treasury of Eastern Han or Tang's Qionlin and Daying stores.

sentences.zh: 願以三十萬緡募保甲為軍。

translations.literal: I wish to use 300,000 strings to recruit baojia as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed spending 300,000 strings to recruit baojia militia as regular troops.

sentences.zh: ”尋用其議。

translations.literal: "Soon his proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，改封樁錢物庫為元祐庫。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 3, the sealed-ledger goods depot was renamed the Yuanyou depot.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou year three, the sealed-ledger depot became the Yuanyou depot.

sentences.zh: 未幾，分元豐庫為元豐南、北庫。

translations.literal: Before long, the Yuanfeng depot was split into Yuanfeng south and north depots.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yuanfeng depot was divided into south and north wings.

sentences.zh: 數月，以北庫為司空呂公著廨，封樁並附南庫仍舊。

translations.literal: Within months the north depot became Minister of Works Lü Gongzhu's office; sealed-ledger goods were again attached to the south depot as before.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the north wing became Minister Lü Gongzhu's offices, and sealed goods returned to the south wing.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詔歲以內藏庫緡錢五十萬樁元豐庫，補助軍費。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng year 6, edict yearly sealed 500,000 strings from the inner treasury into the Yuanfeng depot to supplement military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng year six, the court ordered 500,000 strings yearly from the inner treasury into Yuanfeng for military costs.

sentences.zh: 崇寧以後，諸路封樁禁軍闕額給三路外，與常平、坊場、免役、綢絹、貼輸東北鹽錢，及鬻賣在官田屋錢，應前收樁管封樁權添酒錢、侵占房廊白地錢、公使庫遺利等錢，並輸元豐庫。

translations.literal: After Chongning, aside from sealed funds for metropolitan guard shortfalls on all circuits given to the three frontier circuits, together with ever-normal, monopoly-shop, exemption-service, silk, northeast salt surcharge, and sale of government fields and buildings monies, and former sealed management of added wine tax, occupied corridor and vacant-lot fees, monopoly surplus, and the like—all were sent to the Yuanfeng depot.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongning, ever-normal, franchise, exemption, silk, salt, and property-sale revenues—and countless surcharges on wine, land, and shops—joined sealed metropolitan guard funds flowing to Yuanfeng, except shares reserved for the three frontier circuits.

sentences.zh: 別又置大觀庫，製同元豐，但分東西之別。

translations.literal: Separately the Daguan depot was also established, with regulations like Yuanfeng but divided east and west.
translations.idiomatic: A parallel Daguan depot followed Yuanfeng rules with eastern and western divisions.

sentences.zh: 最後，建宣和庫，有泉貨、弊餘、服禦、玉食、器貢等名，蓋蔡絛欲效王黼以應奉司貢獻要寵，事不足紀。

translations.literal: Finally the Xuanhe depot was built, with designations such as coinage, damaged surplus, apparel, jade food, and tribute vessels—essentially Cai Jing wished to imitate Wang Fu's Supply Commission tributes to win favor; the affair is not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Finally came the Xuanhe depot, labeled for coin, scrap, robes, delicacies, and tribute wares—Cai Jing's imitation of Wang Fu's supply flattery, scarcely worth mention.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔諸路公使庫及神霄宮金銀器皿，所在盡輸元豐庫。

translations.literal: Jingkang year 1, edict ordered public-service depots on all circuits and Shenxiao Palace gold and silver vessels everywhere all sent to the Yuanfeng depot.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang year one, the court seized circuit public-service depots and Shenxiao Palace plate for the Yuanfeng store.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書聶山輒取元豐庫北珠，宰相吳敏白帝，言：“朝廷有元豐、大觀庫，猶陛下有內藏庫。

translations.literal: Revenue Minister Nie Shan rashly took northern pearls from the Yuanfeng depot; Grand Councillor Wu Min informed the emperor, saying: "The court has Yuanfeng and Daguan depots just as Your Majesty has the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue Minister Nie Shan seized Yuanfeng pearls, Councillor Wu Min warned the emperor that Yuanfeng and Daguan were to the court what the inner treasury was to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有闕用，需於內藏，必得旨然後敢取，戶部豈可擅取朝廷庫務物哉？

translations.literal: When the court lacks funds it must draw on the inner treasury and must obtain the imperial directive before daring to take—how can the Revenue Ministry rashly take court depot goods?
translations.idiomatic: Court shortfalls required imperial assent even to touch the inner treasury—Revenue had no right to raid state depots on its own.

sentences.zh: 若人人得擅取庫物，則綱紀亂矣。

translations.literal: If everyone may rashly take depot goods, then discipline is thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If every office looted storehouses at will, public discipline would collapse.

sentences.zh: ”欽宗然之。

translations.literal: "Emperor Qinzong approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 南渡，內藏諸庫貨財之數雖不及前，然兵興用乏，亦時取以為助。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, inner-treasury goods, though not equaling former numbers, were still sometimes drawn on when military expenses were strained.
translations.idiomatic: After the flight south, inner-treasury holdings, though smaller than before, still supplemented wartime shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 其籍帳之詳莫得而考，則以後宋史多闕雲。

translations.literal: The detail of the ledgers cannot be examined, for the later Song History has many lacunae.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed accounts are lost to us, for the later Song History itself survives only in fragments.
